1254.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. In eating, drinking, laughing and sleeping, (the mortal) has forgotten death; forgetting the Master, (he) has brought ruin on himself; cursed is (such) living: no one is to stay (here for ever). O mortal, meditate on the one Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), and go home with your honour. (O God,) what can those who serve you give you? They ask and receive, and cannot do without (asking). You are the Giver of all beings; you alone are the life within beings. Those who meditate (on you) through the Guru receive Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life); they alone become pure. Repeat the Naam night and day, O mortal: (by it) the soiled become clean. As the season is, so is the body's comfort, and such the body becomes. O Nanak, that season alone is lovely (in which the Naam is remembered); without the Name, what season is it? ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
1254.2: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). I make my prayer to my own beloved Guru, that he may bring the Lord, my Husband, and unite (me with him). Hearing the thunder of the clouds, my mind is cooled; dyed in the Beloved's love, (my soul) sings his praises. Rain down, O cloud: my mind is drenched (with love). The drop of Amrit is sweet to (my) heart; the Guru has captivated me, and the mind is absorbed in the Lord's sweet essence. The bride whose mind has come to trust the Guru's words is at peace in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), and dear to her Husband. Taking the Lord as her Husband, the woman has become a happy wife; love brings joy to her mind and body. Casting off her faults, she has become detached; the Lord is her everlasting Husband, her unfailing married joy. Sorrow and separation never take hold of her; the Lord God has shown her his grace. For her there is no coming and going; her mind is steady, for she has taken the shelter of the Perfect Guru. O Nanak, repeating the Name of Ram through the Guru, the bride is a blessed, happy wife in very truth. ॥4॥
1254.3: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With no true awareness in the Naam, they were never satisfied; acting in Haumai (ego), they wasted (their lives). Steeped in the wealth of others, the women of others and slander, they ate poison and suffered pain. They did not recognise the Shabad (the Word) and shed their fears and deceit; in their minds and on their lips is Maya (the world's illusion and lure), only Maya. Loaded with a burden heavy as a python, very heavy, they died and were born again, and wasted their life. When the Shabad pleases the mind, (life) becomes beautiful. Wandering and wandering, (beings) took the guise of many species; those whom the Guru saved found the True One. They did not cast off their anger and bathe at the pilgrims' shrine; the Lord's Name did not please them. They cast away the jewel, the priceless treasure, and abandoned it; they went back to where they came from. They became worms in filth, born of it and absorbed in it again. The more the pleasures, the more the diseases; without the Guru, (they) did not find Sahaj. May my awareness stay in (your) service; may I sing (your) praises in joy, and through the Guru reflect on (divine) knowledge. The seeker is born (to the life of the spirit), the wrangler perishes; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to you, O Guru, O Creator. We were lowly, of shallow mind and false; you are the one who sets (us) right through the Shabad. Where the self is recognised, there you are, to carry across; the True One, the Saviour, carries (beings) across. Seated in a blessed place, may I tell your virtues; which of them can I describe, O Infinite One? The Unseen cannot be seen; you are inaccessible and unborn; you are the one who masters (even) the masters. Looking to whom could I say what you are like? All are beggars; you are the Giver. Nanak, lacking devotion, is at your door: look upon (him); may the one Name be given (to me), that I may keep it in my heart. ॥4॥
1255.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The bride who has not known the taste of (union with) her Husband weeps, her face withered; she has lost hope, caught in the noose of her deeds; without the Guru she has strayed in doubt. Rain down, O cloud: my Husband has come home. I am a sacrifice to my own beloved Guru, who has brought the Lord God and united (me with him). (My) love for the Master is ever new; devotion day and night is lovely. Those to whom the Guru has shown (God's) sight are set free; in every age devotion is beautiful. We are yours, (O God); the world of the three realms is yours; you are mine and I am yours. When the True Guru is met, the Immaculate (Lord) is found; there is no more going round in the world-ocean. When the bride blossoms at the sight of her Husband, the Lord, only then is her adornment true; joined with the Immaculate One, who has no lineage, she is true in the True One; through the Guru's teaching the Naam is her support. She is set free, for the Guru has untied her bonds; with her awareness in the Shabad she has gained honour. O Nanak, the Name of Ram is within her heart; through the Guru (the Lord) has joined her in union (with him). ॥5॥
1255.2: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Another's wife, another's wealth, greed for what is another's, Haumai, vice and wrongdoing, ill will, the slander of others, lust and vile anger: (only) by giving these up (does one find the Amrit within). The Inaccessible, Infinite (Lord) sits within the mansion (of the body); the Amrit within is found only by the one whose conduct is the jewel of the Guru's Shabad. He knows pain and pleasure as one and the same, and so the bad and the good of the world. Understanding, wisdom and awareness are gained through the Lord's Name, in the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), through love for the Guru. Night and day the profit of the Lord's Name is gained; the Guru is the Giver who bestows it. Through the Guru, that teaching is received only by the one on whom the Creator casts his glance of grace. The body is the Lord's mansion, temple and home; in it he has placed his infinite light. O Nanak, through the Guru one is called into the mansion, and the Lord, the Uniter, unites (one with him). ॥4॥
1256.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. One who knows the origin of air and water, who stills the fire (of craving) in the body, if he knows the place from which beings are born, his name is a wise pandit. The virtues of Gobind cannot be known, O mother; he is unseen, and nothing can be said (of him). What can one say to describe him, O mother? (He is) above, below, in the sky and in the nether worlds; how can (he) be described? Reflect, and give (the answer). One who repeats (the Name) in the heart, without the tongue, some such one knows what the Name is like. He grows still, beyond talking and speaking; he alone understands who has (God's) gift. Night and day, within, he keeps his mind lovingly fixed (on God). He alone is a true man who is merged in the True One. If one of high caste and family becomes (God's) servant, then let none of you (try to) speak of (his greatness); (and if) one from among those counted of low caste becomes (God's) servant, then, says Nanak, may he wear shoes (made of my skin). ॥4॥
1256.2: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O physician,) one pain is separation (from God), one pain is hunger; one pain is Death's mighty messengers; one pain is the disease that rushes upon the body. O naive physician, do not apply your medicine. O naive physician, do not apply your medicine. (When) the ache goes on and the pain stays in the body, such medicine has no effect, brother. Forgetting the Master, (one) has indulged in pleasures; then diseases rose up in the body. The blind mind receives (this) punishment: O naive physician, do not apply your medicine. The fruit of sandalwood is the fragrance of sandal; the fruit of a human being is the breath in the body. When the breath has gone, the body collapses; after that no one takes (medicine). Golden is the body, and pure the swan (the soul within), in which is the Naam, a ray of the Immaculate One. (It) has cast off all pain and disease; O Nanak, (it) will be set free through the True Name. ॥4॥
1256.3: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Sorrow is the poison, and the Lord's Name the herb that kills it; let contentment be the grinding slab, and charity in the hand the pestle. Take it every day, and the body does not waste away, (nor) does Death dash (you) down at the end. Take such medicine, O fool, by taking which your vices depart. Rule, riches and youth are all a shade; as the chariot (of the sun) moves round, (only bare) places are seen. Neither body, nor name, nor caste goes (beyond); there it is day; here it is all night. Make your tastes the firewood (of the sacrifice), and craving the ghee and oil; put lust and anger into the fire. (This is) the burnt offering, the sacrifice and the reading of the Puranas; whatever pleases him is accepted. (O God,) austerity is the paper, and your Name the seal (upon it); those for whom this treasure is written are seen to be rich when they reach (the Lord's) home. O Nanak, blessed is the mother who gave (them) birth. ॥4॥
1257.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In white garments, (the crane) speaks her words; (sister,) your nose is long, your eyes black: sister, have you ever seen (your) Master? I fly, and flying I rise into the sky by your strength, O all-powerful Master. On water, on land, on the mountains and the shores I look: in every place is the Master, brother. He who fashioned the body and gave it wings (gave too) great craving, the longing to fly. When he casts his glance of grace, I take heart; as he makes me see, so I see, brother. Neither will this body go (with me), nor will the wings; (it is) a joining of air, water and fire. O Nanak, when (his) grace is there, one meditates (on him), taking the Guru as one's Pir (spiritual guide); (then) this body merges in the True One. ॥4॥
1257.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Formless One is himself the form; he himself leads (beings) astray in doubt. Making and making, the Creator himself watches over it; to whatever pleases him he sets (each one). This is the greatness of the servant whom he makes obey his Hukam (God's will and command). (God) himself knows his own will; by the Guru's grace it is understood. (Then) this Shakti comes home to Shiv, and one stays dead while yet alive. (The pandit) reads the Vedas and, having read, expounds disputes about Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh. This is the Maya of the three qualities, which has led the world astray; (in it is) the dread of birth and death. One who by the Guru's grace knows the One, from his mind anxiety is gone. (O God,) we are lowly, foolish and thoughtless; take care of us yourself. Be merciful, make (me) the servant of your servants, that I may serve you. Give (me) your one treasure, that night and day I may speak the Naam. Says Nanak, understand by the Guru's grace; (only) a rare one reflects thus: as foam and bubbles on water, so is this world. It merges into the One from whom it came, and the whole expanse is gone. ॥4॥
Shiv and Shakti: here Shiv is the Lord, the source of good, and Shakti is Maya. The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas.
1258.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who have recognised the Hukam, (God) has united (with himself), burning away their Haumai through the Shabad. They perform true devotion night and day, and keep their minds lovingly fixed on the True One. Through the Guru's Shabad, in loving ease, they ever behold the True Lord (close at hand). O mind, accept the Hukam: (by it) there is peace. His own will is pleasing to God; the one he forgives meets no obstacle. The three qualities are all a running about; (in them) there is neither devotion to the Lord nor love. (For such) there is never a higher state, nor liberation, for they do their deeds in Haumai. Whatever pleases the Master comes to pass; (beings) wander by the deeds already done. When the True Guru is met, the mind stays dead (to itself), and the Lord's Name comes to dwell in the mind. His worth cannot be reckoned; nothing at all can be said (of him). He comes to dwell in the fourth state, and stays merged in the True One. My Lord God is inaccessible, beyond the senses; his worth cannot be told. By the Guru's grace one understands (him), doing one's work by the Shabad. O Nanak, praise the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and gain glory at (his) door. ॥4॥
The fourth state (turiya): the spiritual state beyond Maya's three qualities.
1258.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Rare is the one who understands through the Guru, the one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace: there is no giver but the Guru; casting his glance of grace, he forgives. When the Guru is met, peace wells up, and (one) takes the Naam day and night. O my mind, meditate on the Lord's Amrit Name. When the True Guru, the Being, is met, the Name is found, and one stays merged in the Lord's Name for ever. The manmukhs (the self-willed) wander, ever separated (from God); no one stands by anyone. Haumai is a great disease; Jamkaal (death) has struck them on the head. Those who take the Guru's teaching are not parted from the Sat Sangat, and cherish the Naam day and night. (O God,) you alone are the Creator of all; ever you make (them), and watch over and consider (them). Some you yourself have united (with you) through the Guru, and bestowed (on them) the treasures of devotion. You yourself know everything; before whom (else) should I cry out? The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is Amrit; it is found by (his) glance of grace. (Such a one) utters Har Har day and night, in the Sahaj given by the Guru, with love. O Nanak, the Naam is the treasure; fix your mind on the Naam alone. ॥4॥
1258.3: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). I praise the Guru for ever, the Giver of peace; he is God, Narayan himself. (One who) by the Guru's grace has reached the supreme state has been given great glory; day and night he ever sings the praises of the True One, and he merges in the True One. O mind, reflect (on him) in the heart, through the Guru. Give up falsehood, (attachment to) family, Haumai, and craving that is poison; keep in your heart that you must depart. The True Guru is the Giver of the Name of Ram; there is no other giver. (Those to whom) he gives the gift of (spiritual) life are satisfied, and merge in the True Name. Day and night the Lord pervades their hearts, and they stay in the samadhi of Sahaj. (When) this mind is pierced by the True Guru's Shabad, the true Bani (dwells) in the heart. My God is unseen and cannot be seen; through the Guru the story of the Indescribable (is told). (When) the Giver of peace himself shows mercy, (then) one meditates on Saringpani (the Lord who bears the bow). There is no more coming and going (for one who) has meditated in Sahaj through the Guru. From within the mind itself the mind has met the Master, and the mind is merged within the mind. Only the True One is truth; (the mind) is won over by the True One, having lost its self-conceit from within. The one and only Master dwells in the mind; there is no second, none other. The one Name is sweet Amrit; in the world it alone is the pure truth. O Nanak, the Name is received from God, by those for whom it is so written from the beginning. ॥5॥
1259.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The ganas and gandharvas were all saved through the Naam, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. Killing Haumai, they enshrined (the Name) in the mind for ever, and kept the Lord fixed in the heart. He alone understands whom (God) makes understand, whom he himself unites (with himself). Day and night he sings (God's praise) through the Bani and the Shabad, and keeps his mind lovingly fixed on the True One. O my mind, cherish the Naam each moment. The Guru's gift, the peace of the Shabad, (is) within, and stays with you for ever. The manmukh's hypocrisy never ends; in the love of another he suffers pain. Forgetting the Naam, his mind steeped in the poison (of Maya), he wastes his life in vain. This chance does not come to hand again; day and night he is ever repenting. He dies and dies and is born again, never understanding, and is absorbed in filth. Those who through the Guru are steeped in the Naam are saved, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. Liberated while yet alive, they meditated on the Lord's Name and kept the Lord fixed in the heart. Their mind and body are pure, their understanding pure and noble, and their speech has become noble too. They have known the one Being, the one God; there is no second, none other. God himself does, and himself causes to be done; he himself casts his glance of grace. Mind and body are steeped in the Guru's Bani, and awareness is absorbed in service. The Unseen, the Unfathomable dwells within; becoming Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru), one sees him. O Nanak, to the one who pleases him he himself gives (this gift); as it pleases him, so he makes (beings) walk. ॥4॥
Ganas are the attendants of the gods, gandharvas the singers of the heavens.
1259.2: Raag Malar, Dutuke, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). From the True Guru one finds (God's) home, his door, his mansion, that place; through the Guru's Shabad, pride is ended. Those on whose foreheads the Naam is written from the beginning meditate on the Naam day and night, for ever and ever, and receive honour in the true court. One who learns the ways of the mind from the True Guru has his attention fixed on the Lord day and night, for ever. Steeped in the Guru's Shabad, they stay ever detached, and receive honour in the Lord's true court. This mind plays, bound by the Hukam; in an instant it roams the ten directions and comes back. When the true Lord God himself casts his glance of grace, then through the Guru this mind comes under control at once. The ways of this mind one comes to know from the mind itself, understanding by reflecting on the Shabad. O Nanak, meditate on the Naam always, by which you will cross the ocean of the world. ॥4॥
Dutuke: hymns whose every stanza has two tuks (each a verse in two halves).
1260.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Soul, body and breath are all his; he pervades every heart. Apart from the One I know no other; the True Guru has given (me) this understanding. O my mind, I keep myself lovingly fixed on the Naam; the Unseen, beyond the senses, the Infinite Creator, the Lord: through the Guru's Shabad I meditate on him. Mind and body are drenched when love is fixed on the One, and one stays merged in Sahaj. By the Guru's grace doubt and fear flee, when love is fixed on the one Name. When one does the work of truth by the Guru's words, only then is the higher state, and (true) understanding, gained. Among millions, (God) gives understanding to some rare one; that one has fixed his love on the Name of Ram. Wherever I look, there is the One alone; this understanding I have gained through the Guru's teaching. I place mind, body and breath before him; Nanak sheds his self. ॥4॥
1260.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). My God is true, the Remover of sorrow; he is found through the Shabad. Steeped in devotion, they stay ever detached, and have gained honour at the true door. O mind, (so) I stay merged within the mind; through the Guru the mind is drenched in the Name of Ram, and love stays fixed on the Lord. My God is utterly inaccessible, beyond the senses; through the Guru's teaching he gives understanding. (For such a one) truth is the self-discipline, the Lord's praise the way of life, and love stays fixed on the Lord. The True One himself is the Shabad, himself the teaching, (for those) who have merged their light in the Light. The body is frail, and the breath plays it; through the Guru, Amrit is received. He himself fashions, and sets all to their work; that True One pervades (all). O Nanak, without the Name no one is anything; through the Name (God) gives glory. ॥4॥
1260.3: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The poison of Haumai has bewitched the mind, which is loaded with a burden heavy as a python. (One who) put the Shabad, the Garur (antidote), in his mouth, the Lord has killed his poison of Haumai. O mind, Haumai and attachment are a heavy pain; this world, this world-ocean, cannot be crossed (with them); through the Guru, cross over in the boat of (the Name of) the Lord. The spread of attachment to Maya of the three qualities is at work in all that has form. The quality of turiya is found in the Sat Sangat; the Gracious One carries (one) across. (As) the scent of sandalwood is fragrant, and its rich fragrance spreads far, (so) the way of life of the Lord's servants is noble; they spread the Lord's praise in the world. Show grace, show grace, O my Master: set the Lord, Har Har Har, in (my) heart. O Nanak, (one who) has found the Perfect True Guru has repeated in the mind the Name of Murari (the foe of the demon Mur, God). ॥4॥
Garur: a remedy against snake venom, named after Garuda, the bird who is the enemy of snakes; it was ground on a stone and taken by mouth.
1261.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Is this mind a householder, or is it an udasi (one who has renounced the world)? Or is this mind beyond caste, ever imperishable? Is this mind restless, or is this mind dispassionate? From where has possessiveness come to cling to this mind? O pandit, reflect on this mind; why read so much else? (You only) carry a load. The Creator has fastened the possessiveness of Maya (on beings); issuing this Hukam, he brought forth the creation. By the Guru's grace understand (this), brothers, and stay for ever in the Lord's refuge. He alone is a pandit who sets down the bundle of the three qualities, and day and night speaks the one Naam. He takes the True Guru's teaching, (and) lays his head before the True Guru. He stays ever apart, free of desire; such a pandit is accepted in the (Lord's) court. He proclaims the One, the only One, in all; when he sees the One alone, then he knows the One alone. The one whom he forgives, he unites (with himself); (for him) there is peace for ever, here and hereafter. Says Nanak, what way can anyone take, what can anyone do? He alone is freed on whom (God's) grace falls; he sings the Lord's praises day and night, and then the Shastras and the Vedas no longer cry out (to him). ॥5॥
1261.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Wandering and wandering, the manmukh is made to roam through the species; Jamkaal strikes (him) every day; (he) has lost his honour. Serving the True Guru has ended subjection to Jam; the Lord God is met, and (his) mansion, (his) home, is found. O mortal, meditate on the Naam through the Guru. The treasure of human birth, lost in double-mindedness, goes for a shell. When (God) shows grace, love (for him) takes hold through the Guru; (O mortal,) enshrine devotion to the Lord, Har Har, within, in your heart. (He) is the one who carries (one) across the world-ocean through the Shabad; (such a one) is seen to be true at the true door. (Those who) performed many rites but did not find the True Guru have strayed in doubt without the Guru, in much Maya; they have swelled their Haumai, possessiveness and great attachment; in the love of another the manmukh has suffered pain. The Creator himself is inaccessible and unfathomable; through the Guru's Shabad one should meditate (on him): (this is) the true profit. The Lord, free of all need, is present, here before us. O Nanak, through the Guru (one) merges in the Naam. ॥4॥
1262.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who hold to the Guru's teaching are liberated while yet alive; in devotion to the Lord they stay awake, night and day, for ever. Shedding their self, they serve the True Guru; I ever fall at the feet of those servants (of God). I live, ever singing of the Lord's virtues; the Guru's Shabad is sweet, of supreme relish; through the Lord's Name I have gained liberation, the higher state. Attachment to Maya is ignorance, pitch darkness; the foolish, ignorant manmukhs are enticed (by it). Day and night (their life) goes by as they busy themselves with worldly affairs; they die and die and are born again, and punishment comes to them. The Gurmukh keeps his mind lovingly fixed on the Name of Ram; he does not cling to the greed for what is false. Whatever comes to pass, (he accepts it) in Sahaj, with love; he drinks the Lord's sweet essence, savouring it with his tongue. Among millions, (God) gives understanding to some rare one; he himself forgives, and gives glory. One who is united (with him) from the beginning is not parted (from him); O Nanak, (he) stays merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1262.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Everyone utters the Naam with the tongue; (but) only if one serves the True Guru does one find the Naam. He breaks his bonds and dwells in the home of liberation; through the Guru's Shabad he sits, steady, in his own home. O my mind, why should one be resentful? In Kalyug (the dark age) the Name of Ram is the profit; through the Guru's teaching one should cherish it in the heart, night and day. The rain-bird cries out moment by moment; without seeing the Beloved, it gets no sleep; this separation cannot be borne. When the True Guru is met, then (the Beloved) is met, with ease and love. One without the Naam perishes and suffers pain; burnt by craving, he is not rid of his hunger. Without good fortune the Naam is not found; (one) grows weary performing rites in many ways. (Caught) in the three qualities, (one) reflects on the words of the Vedas; (on him is) the filth of the poison (of Maya), and in that poison is his trade; (such people) die and are born, and are ruined again and again. Through the Guru, enshrine in your heart the quality of turiya. One who honours the Guru is honoured by everyone; through the Guru's words (his) mind grows cool. In all four ages (he has) glory; that servant is pure. O Nanak, rare is (such) a Gurmukh. ॥5॥
The babiha (papiha, the rain-bird) is said to drink only drops of rain, and to keep calling out for them.
1262.3: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Night and day I have meditated on the Lord, Har Har, in my heart; with an understanding shaped by the Guru's teaching, I have put sorrow out of mind. The bonds of all hopes and desires have broken; the Lord God, Har Har, has shown grace. My eyes are fixed in a steady gaze on the Lord, Har Har; seeing the True Guru my mind has blossomed: the servant has met the Lord, Banwari. The one who has forgotten such a Name of my Lord, Har Har: a stain has fallen on his family. O Lord, let no birth take place in his family; make his mother a widow. O Lord, Har Har, bring and unite (me with) the holy Guru, who keeps the Lord in his heart day and night. When the Guru is seen, the Guru's Sikh blossoms, as a child does on seeing its mother. The bride and the Husband dwell together in one (place), but between (them) stands the hard wall of Haumai. The Perfect Guru has broken down the wall of Haumai, and servant Nanak has met Banwari. ॥4॥
Banwari (he of the forest garland) is a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani it is a name of God.
1263.1: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Ganga, the Jamuna, the Godavari and the Saraswati: these strive for the dust of (the feet of) the Saadh (the holy one). (They say:) Filled with the filth of sins, (people) plunge into us; the dust of the Saadh's feet takes away our filth. (It is as if) I have bathed at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage: the dust of the Sat Sangat has flown up and fallen into (my) eyes, and has taken away all the filth of evil-mindedness. The Jahnavi (the Ganga) was brought down by the austerity of Bhagirath; Kedar was established by Mahesh; Kashi, and (the land where) Krishna grazed the cows: (these) gained glory by meeting the Lord's servants. As many places of pilgrimage as the gods have established, every one of them longs for the dust of the Saadh's feet. When the Lord's Sant, the holy Guru, meets them, they take the dust of his feet and put it on their faces. However vast your creation, O my Master, all of it longs for the dust of the Saadh's feet. O Nanak, the one on whose forehead it is written: to him the Lord gives the Saadh's dust, and carries him across. ॥4॥

The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are the tiraths held most holy in India. Jahnavi: the Ganga; by the Puranic story, King Bhagirath brought the Ganga down from heaven to the earth. Kedar (Kedarnath): a shrine of Shiva high in the Himalayas, held to be a place of pilgrimage. Kashi (Banaras) is Shiva's city; Krishna grazed the cows in Brindaban.
1263.2: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). To that servant the Lord tastes sweet, on whom the Lord, Har Har, shows grace. The one who utters the Lord's praises is rid of hunger and of every pain. O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har Har: (by it, one) is saved. One who hears the Guru's words with his ears and meditates crosses the world-ocean. I am a slave bought in the market by that servant on whom the Lord, Har Har, shows grace. Meeting the Lord's servant, one finds peace; he takes away all the filth of evil-mindedness. The Lord's servant hungers for the Lord; the servant is satisfied when he reflects on the Lord's virtues. The Lord's servant is a fish whose water is the Lord; forgetting the Lord, he bursts and dies. He who has kindled this love knows it, or the one in whose mind he places it. Servant Nanak finds peace on seeing the Lord, and all the hunger of his body departs. ॥4॥
1263.3: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). As many beings and creatures as God has made, on the head of each he writes its work. To his servant the Lord has given glory: the Lord sets his servant to the Lord's work. The True Guru makes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm (within). Speak (the Name of) the Lord, Sikhs of the Guru, my brothers: the Lord carries the world across the fearsome world-ocean. The servant who worships the Guru and serves him is dear to my Lord God. Worship the True Guru: (this is) the Lord's service; showing grace, (God) himself carries (one) across. Gone astray in doubt, the ignorant and blind wander and wander, and have flowers plucked (for worship); they worship the lifeless and bow at tombs; (such a one) wastes all his labour in vain. He who knows God should be called the True Guru; he makes (all) hear the story of the Lord, Har Har. Before that Guru set, with faith, clothes and food, silks and fine robes of many kinds; the merit of that never runs short. The True Guru is the Divine One, the manifest image of the Lord, who speaks words of Amrit. O Nanak, good is the fortune of that servant who fixes his mind on the Lord's feet. ॥5॥
1264.1: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those in whose hearts my True Guru dwells are Sants, good in every way. At the sight of them my mind blossoms; I am ever a sacrifice to them. O wise one, speak (the Name of) the Lord day and night. All the craving and hunger of those is gone who, through the Guru's teaching, eat the sweet essence of Ram. The Lord's servants, the Saadhs, are (true) friends, meeting whom doubt is removed. As the swan picks out water from milk and sets them apart, so the Saadh picks out Haumai and envy and drives them from the body. Those who have no love for the Lord in their hearts are deceitful men; they ever practise deceit. What can anyone give them, what can he feed them? They themselves sow, and they themselves eat. The mark of the Lord is the very mark of the Lord's servant; the Lord himself places himself within his servant. Blessed, blessed is Guru Nanak, who sees all alike, who has crossed beyond slander and praise, and carries (others) across. ॥4॥
1264.2: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's Name is inaccessible, beyond the senses, and sublime; by the Lord's grace I have repeated it. By great good fortune I have found the Sat Sangat of the Saadh; in the Saadh's company I have crossed over. Bliss has come to my mind, night and day; by the Guru's grace I have repeated the Lord's Name, and the doubt and fear of my mind are gone. Those who have sung of the Lord, those who have repeated (his Name): O Lord, in your mercy, unite (me with) their company. Beholding them, I have found peace; pain and the disease of Haumai are gone. Those who meditate on the Naam in the heart night and day: their whole life has borne fruit. They themselves have crossed over and carried the whole world across, and their whole family too has crossed over. (O God,) you yourself made the whole world, and you yourself have brought it under your sway. God has shown grace to servant Nanak, and pulled him out as he was drowning in poison. ॥4॥
1265.1: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (One who) has not drunk the Amrit by the Guru's grace is not rid of craving and hunger. The foolish manmukh burns in pride, and suffers pain in Haumai. Coming and going, he has wasted his life in vain; when pain strikes, he repents. They do not remember the One from whom they came: cursed is (such) living, cursed (such) eating. O mortal, meditate on the Naam through the Guru. (On whom) the Lord, Har Har, shows grace, him he unites with the Guru, and he merges in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. The manmukh's life has gone to waste; coming and going, he is put to shame. The proud are drowned in lust and anger; (such a one) burns away in Haumai. They gain neither spiritual attainment nor understanding; their mind is dull, and in the waves of greed they suffer pain. Without the Guru they have suffered great pain; seized by the messengers of Jam, they wail. (He) has found the Lord's Name, which is beyond the senses, through the Guru, in Sahaj, with love. The treasure of the Naam has come to dwell within his heart, and his tongue sings the Lord's praises. He stays ever in bliss, day and night, his mind lovingly fixed on the one Shabad. In Sahaj he has found the treasure of the Naam; this is the greatness of the True Guru. It is from the True Guru that the Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell in my mind; ever am I a sacrifice to the True Guru. Offering mind and body, I place everything before (him), and fix my mind on the Guru's feet. Show your grace, O Perfect Guru, and yourself take me into union. We are iron; the Guru is the boat, the ship, that carries Nanak across. ॥4॥
1265.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 3, Partal, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Lord's servants speak the Name of Sri Ram, joining your Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), O Lord. Trade in the Lord's wealth, gather the Lord's wealth, on which no thief can lay a hand. The chatrik (rain-bird) and the peacock call out day and night, hearing the thunder of the clouds. Whatever deer, fish and birds call out, they repeat no other but the Lord. O Nanak, for the servants who have sung the Lord's praise, all the clamour of Jam is ended. ॥4॥
Partal: a setting in which the rhythm (taal) changes again and again as the hymn is sung.
1265.3: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Uttering Ram, Ram again and again, the fortunate search (for him). If anyone shows (me) the Lord's path, I fall at his feet. The Lord is my friend and helper; my love is fixed on the Lord. I sing of the Lord, I speak of the Lord; any other love, of duality, I have given up. My Beloved, who enchants the mind, is Ram, the Lord, supreme bliss, beyond attachment. Nanak lives by seeing the Lord, if for a single moment, an instant, (his) face is seen. ॥2॥
1266.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. What are you worrying about, what are you thinking over, what schemes are you making? Say, what need has he to care about anyone, whose helper is Gopal (the Lord who sustains all)? The cloud is raining, O friend; the Guest has come to (my) home. O Master, treasure of grace, (keep) me, the lowly, merged in the Name, the nine treasures. I have made many foods of many kinds, many dishes and sweets; I have made the kitchen clean and pure; now, O Lord, my King, partake (of them). The wicked (the five enemies) are destroyed, the friends (the virtues) rejoice; (the Lord) has made these temples, these homes (of the body), his own. When the playful Beloved came into my home, then I found every comfort. In the assembly of the Sants (I have) the shelter of the Perfect Guru; from the beginning this writ was written on (my) forehead. Servant Nanak has found the playful Husband; sorrow does not come to touch (him) again. ॥4॥
1266.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When a child lives on milk, it cannot do without milk; (when) the mother tends it with care and puts (milk) into its mouth, then it is fed and content. We are children; God, the Giver, is (our) father. Children go wrong many times, hundreds of thousands of times; (yet) there is no other place where they could go. The poor child's mind is fickle; it puts its hands to snakes and fire; the mother and father keep it held to their bosom, and then it plays in bliss and ease. O my Master, the child whose father you are: what hunger can it know? In your house are the nine treasures, the treasure of the Name; whatever (the child) longs for in his mind, he will receive. The merciful Father has given this command: whatever the child asks with his mouth is to be given. Nanak, the child, longs for the sight of God: may (your) feet ever dwell in my heart. ॥4॥
1266.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Applying myself in every way, I have made preparation, and cast off all anxiety; I have begun all the work of the house, relying on the Master. Lovely music is heard playing. The dawn has come: I have seen my Beloved's face, and in my home are lovely songs of joy. Applying my mind, I have made the places beautiful; I go and ask the Sants. Searching and searching I have met the Guest; bowing at (his) feet, I worship him. When the Beloved came and settled on the seat in my home, then I sang the song of joy. My friends and companions grew happy: the Guru has united (me with) God, the Perfect One. My friends and companions are in bliss; the Guru has brought my tasks to fulfilment. Says Nanak, I have met the Groom, the Giver of peace, who does not leave me and go far away. ॥4॥
1267.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). From king to worm, from worm to the lord of the gods (Indra), (all) fill their bellies by doing wrong. Forsaking the Treasure of grace, they worship others; they are slayers of their own souls, and thieves. Forgetting the Lord, they die in pain upon pain. Many times over they wander through many species, and can lean on no one. Those who forsake the Master and set their thoughts on another are fools, dullards, wretches and asses. In a paper boat, how can they cross the sea? In vain they say that they are crossing. Shiva, Biranchi (Brahma), demons and gods, as many as there are, burn in the fire of death. Nanak (seeks) the refuge of your lotus feet: do not cast (him) away, O God, the Creator. ॥3॥
1267.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those who are my God's own are detached, and have renounced (all); I cannot stay a moment without him; my love is fixed (on him). In their company God comes to my mind; by the Sants' grace I have awoken. Hearing (their) teaching, minds have become pure; dyed in (his) love, (I) have sung (his) praises. Giving this mind, I have made the Sants my friends; by great good fortune, they have shown me mercy. I have found a great peace that I cannot describe; Nanak has gained the dust of the feet of (God's) servants. ॥2॥
Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
1267.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, unite me with my Beloved. All the friends in whose homes the Beloved dwells sleep, filled with peace. In me are faults, (yet) God is ever merciful; I am without virtue: what cleverness have I? I set myself up as the equal of those who are steeped in the Beloved's love: this is the brazenness of Haumai. Grown humble, I have looked to the one refuge of the Guru, the True Guru, the Being, the Giver of peace. In a single instant he has cut away all my pain; Nanak's night passes in peace. ॥2॥
1267.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Rain down, O dear cloud; do not delay even a little. Rain, O beloved, support of my mind, that there may be bliss, and joy in the mind for ever. I lean on your support, O my Master: why do you put (me) out of your mind? (I am) a woman, like a maidservant: without the Husband there is no glory. When my Master heard my prayer, he came quickly, showing grace. Says Nanak, my married bliss is made: (I have) honour, glory and good conduct. ॥2॥
1268.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meditate on the true Name of the Beloved. The world-ocean of pain and sorrow comes to an end: enshrine the Guru's form in your heart. Enemies are struck down and all who wish ill are afflicted, (for one who) has come to the Lord's refuge; the Saviour has given (him) his hand and protected (him), and (he) has found the treasure of the Naam. Showing grace, (God) has cut away all sins, and given the pure Naam in the mind. O Nanak, the Treasure of virtues has come to dwell in the mind, and sorrow does not come again. ॥2॥
The Guru's form (moorat): in Gurbani the Guru's form is his Word, the Shabad.
1268.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my God, my Beloved, dear as life, O Merciful One, showing grace, give (me) loving devotion and your own Name. I remember your feet, O Beloved; in (my) heart is hope in you. I make my prayer to the Sants; in (my) mind is a thirst for (your) sight. Separation is death, and meeting the Lord is life: grant your servant (your) sight. The Name is Nanak's support, the wealth of (his) life: O my God, show grace. ॥2॥
1268.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Now I have come into accord with my own Beloved. Remembering Ram, the King, I have found peace: rain down, O cloud, Giver of peace. I do not forget the Ocean of peace for even a moment; I have found the Naam, the nine treasures. My full destiny has come to light: I have met the Sant, my helper. Peace has sprung up, all sorrows are destroyed, and my mind is lovingly fixed on the Supreme Lord. I have crossed the world, the hard and fearful ocean: Nanak meditates on the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
1268.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The cloud has rained and spread over the whole world; my beloved God has become merciful, and (I) have found bliss, joy and peace. Troubles are erased and all craving quenched, (for I) have meditated on the Supreme Lord in (my) mind. In the Saadh Sangat births and deaths are ended, and (I) have not wandered anywhere again. Mind and body are dyed in the Name of the Immaculate One, and lovingly fixed on (his) lotus feet. My own God has taken (me) as his own; Nanak, (his) servant, has come to (his) refuge. ॥2॥
1268.5: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). How could they live a life apart (from him), in whose minds is the yearning and hope of meeting (him), of drinking the nectar of (his) lotus feet? Those who thirst for you, O Beloved, have no distance (from you); those who forget my beloved Ram are dead, and go on dying. The Lord of the world pervades (their) minds and bodies; they see him ever present. O Nanak, he pervades within all; he fills everything to the full. ॥2॥
1269.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through worship of the Lord, whom has (he) not carried across? Those in the bodies of birds, of fish, of deer and of boars have been saved in the Saadh's company. The races of gods and of demons, yakshas and kinnars (beings of the heavens) and men have crossed the ocean. Whoever worships (the Lord) in the Saadh's company, his sorrows are destroyed. Lust, anger and the pleasures of the great poison (of Maya): from these they have become free. They repeat (the Name of) the Lord who is kind to the meek and full of compassion; Nanak is a sacrifice (to them) for ever. ॥2॥
1269.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Today I have sat down in the Lord's shop. Sharing the capital of the Naam with (his) servants, I do not go to the landing of Jam. Showing grace, the Supreme Lord has saved (me), and the doors of doubt have opened. I have found God, the Banker beyond reckoning, and earned the profit, the treasure of (his) feet. I have taken hold of the refuge of the Unshakeable, Imperishable One, and (my) sins have been picked out and cast away. The strife and sorrows of servant Nanak are ended; he does not fall into the species again. ॥2॥
1269.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In many ways (beings) are robbed by attachment to Maya. Among millions, rare is the servant who has long been a perfect devotee. Wavering here and there, he has gained (only) toil; body and wealth become another's. Hiding from people he practises deceit, and does not recognise the One who is with him. Deer, bird and fish, lowly and base: into these troubles he comes again. Says Nanak, O God, carry (us) stones across, that (we) may enjoy peace in the Saadh Sangat. ॥2॥
1269.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The wicked have died, having eaten poison, O mother; he whose creatures they are has himself protected them; my God has been moved to grace. The Knower of hearts is at work in all; then what fear can there be, brother? He is with (us), our helper, and does not leave and go; God is seen in every place. The Master of the masterless, Destroyer of the pain of the meek, has himself fastened (us) to the hem of his robe. Your servants live by the Lord's shelter; Nanak is in God's refuge. ॥2॥
1269.5: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O my mind, one should dwell on the Lord's feet. Thirst for (his) sight has enticed my mind: one should put on wings and meet the Lord. Searching and searching I have found the way: one should serve the Saadh. Show grace, O my Master, that the Naam, the great nectar, may be drunk. Crying, Save (me), save (me), I have come to (your) refuge: show grace to (me), who am burning. Take your servant by the hand; make Nanak your own. ॥2॥
1270.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). To be the Lover of devotion is God's innate nature. He has struck down the slanderers and put them beneath (his devotees') feet, and spread his own glory. He has caused acclaim to ring through all the world, and put compassion into (all) beings. Holding his servant to his bosom, he has protected him, and not let even a hot wind touch him. My Master has taken (me) as his own; erasing doubt and fear, he has given (me) peace. O servants of the Lord, rejoice in supreme bliss; O Nanak, faith has come into the mind. ॥2॥
1270.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Through the Guru, (the world) is seen to be God's expanse; through the Guru, (it is seen as) the spread of the three qualities; through the Guru is the understanding of the Naad (the yogis' sound) and the Vedas; without the Perfect Guru there is pitch darkness. O my mind, calling on the Guru, one finds lasting peace. Through the Guru's teaching the Lord has come to dwell in the heart; with every breath and morsel one should meditate on one's Master. I am a sacrifice to the Guru's feet; I sing the Guru's praises night and day, always; in the dust of the Guru's (feet) I bathe; (so) honour is received in the true court. The Guru is the ship that carries (us) across the world-ocean; when the Guru is met, there is no more birth into the species. That servant alone gains the Guru's service, for whom it has come written, by (God's) grace, from the beginning. The Guru is my life, the Guru my support; the Guru is my daily provision, the Guru my family; the Guru is my Master; (I am) in the True Guru's refuge. O Nanak, the Guru is the Supreme Lord, whose worth cannot be told. ॥4॥
1270.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have enshrined the Guru's feet in my heart; showing grace, God himself has united (me with him). God joins his own servant (to himself); the worth of that (servant) cannot be told. Show grace, O Perfect One, Giver of peace. By your grace alone you come to mind, and (your servants) stay dyed in your love at all hours. Singing and hearing (your praise): all of it is your will; one who understands (your) Hukam merges in the True One. (Your servants) live by repeating your Name again and again; without you there is no other place (for them). Pain and pleasure are the Creator's Hukam, his will; by his will he forgives, by his will he gives punishment. He himself is the Maker of both ends (forgiveness and punishment); I am a sacrifice to your glory, (O God). Your worth you alone know; you yourself understand, and you yourself hear and tell (of it). They alone are devotees who are pleasing to you; Nanak is a sacrifice to them for ever. ॥4॥
1271.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme God has become merciful; the cloud rains down streams of Amrit. All beings and creatures are satisfied; (their) tasks have come out wholly right. O mind, ever and ever cherish the Naam, which is found by serving the Perfect Guru, and stands by (you) here and hereafter. The Destroyer of fears has shattered sorrow; he has taken care of his own beings. The Saviour is ever kind; ever and ever one should be a sacrifice (to him). The Creator himself has done away with death; O mind, ever and ever repeat (the Name of) him. Casting (his) glance (of grace), he has kept all creatures safe; sing the praises of the Lord, day after day. The One Creator is all by himself; the Lord's devotees know (his) glory. He has always kept the honour of his Name; Nanak speaks as he makes him speak. ॥4॥
1271.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the Guru's refuge are all treasures; (there) honour is received in the true court. Doubt, fear, pain and sorrow all depart by ever singing the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat. O my mind, praise the Perfect Guru. Repeat the Naam, the treasure, day and night; (so one) obtains the fruits the mind longs for. No other is as great as the True Guru; that very Guru is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God. (He) saves from the pain of birth and death; (one he saves) never tastes the poison of Maya again. The Guru's greatness is beyond telling; absorbed in the true Name, the Guru is (the form of) the Supreme God. True is (his) discipline, and all (his) deeds are true; pure is that mind which is absorbed in the Guru's company. The Perfect Guru is found by great good fortune; cast lust, anger and greed out of your mind. Showing grace, (O God,) give (me) a dwelling at the Guru's feet; Nanak's prayer (to you), O God, is for (the gift of) the Truth. ॥4॥
1271.3: Raag Malar, Ghar 3, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Winning the Guru's favour, I have made love with the merciful Beloved. I have put on all my adornments, O friend; I have cast off all vices, O friend; (my) wandering (mind) has become steady. O mind, you too, finding (him) in this way, shed self-conceit and keep company with the Saadhs. (Then, within,) the drums and other instruments play unstruck; O friend, (the tongue,) like the koel, utters the Name of Ram in sweet words, and is most lovely. Such is the glory of your sight, O Beloved, boundless beyond measure and never in vain; in (your) company the Sants too become like (you). They utter the Name that carries (one) across the world; the rosary of the Name of Ram, who pervades all, (those who) turn in their minds become companions of the Lord. O servant Nanak, the Beloved grows dear (to them). ॥2॥
1272.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (My) mind wanders in the dense forest; it goes on, eager and yearning, with the longing to meet God. Maya of the three qualities has come to beguile me; to whom shall I tell (my) pain? I have tried every other remedy, (but they) cannot take away the pain. O Nanak, hasten to the refuge of the Saadh, and plunging into the virtues of Gobind, meet (him). ॥2॥
1272.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Lovely and fine is the glory of the Beloved. Haha, Huhu and the other gandharvas, and the apsaras, sing (of him) finely, with bliss, gladness and delight. Masters of the art sound sweet strains in many ways, and show fine forms of many kinds. Mountains, trees, dry land, waters and worlds (he) fills; in every heart the Beloved's dwelling is fine. O Nanak, one in whose (heart) is fine faith has found the delight of the lovely Lord in the Saadh Sangat. ॥2॥
Apsaras are the dancers of the heavens.
1272.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through love for the Guru, (I) have enshrined the Beloved's lotus feet in my heart. Fruitful is (his) sight: beholding it, sins have gone, (all) gone; minds have become pure and full of light. (I) am astonished, amazed, lost in wonder; by taking the Name, millions of sins are destroyed. Laying my forehead at the Guru's feet, I have fallen (before him). O God, you alone are, you alone. Your devotees have your support alone; servant Nanak is at (your) door, in (your) refuge. ॥2॥
1272.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Rain down with joy, (O cloud,) at (God's) command, that there be bliss, and all good fortune (awaken). In the company of the Sants the mind blossoms, (as) the earth, meeting the cloud, is a happy bride. The peacock loves the thunder of the clouds; the chatrik's heart is set on the (rain)drop. Such, O mind, (let your) love be for the Lord, (and) cast off the deceit of Maya. Meeting the Sants, Nanak has awoken. ॥2॥
1272.5: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sing the praises of Gopal every day; keep the Name of Ram in your mind. Giving up pride, casting off arrogance, joining the company of the Saadhs, remember the Lord with single-minded love, O friend, and (your) faults are erased. The Supreme Lord has become merciful; the entanglements of the senses' pleasures are destroyed. Clinging to the feet of the Saadhs, Nanak sings (the praises of) Gobind every day. ॥2॥
1272.6: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The cloud, the form of Gobind (the Guru), thunders; singing (his) praises brings peace and rest. The refuge of the Lord's feet is (the boat) to cross the ocean; (there is) the unstruck melody, and words full of delight. The thirsty traveller's mind is set on the pool, to take the water of the spirit. Servant Nanak loves the sight of the Lord; God, showing grace, grants (it). ॥2॥
1273.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Gobind, O Gopal, O merciful Beloved, Master of the breath of life, Friend of the masterless, Dispeller of the pain of the meek, O All-powerful, Unreachable, Perfect One, show me mercy. Carry Nanak across, out of the most dreadful blind well (of the world). ॥3॥
1273.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The chakvi's eyes do not long for sleep; without her mate she gets no sleep. When the sun comes up, her eyes behold her beloved, and she bows down again and again at his feet. The Husband's love is pleasing (to me); (it is my) companion. Without him I do not live in the world for a moment; such is the thirst that has seized me. The lotus in the pool blossoms of its own nature, with ease, at the ray (of the sun) in the sky. Such love for the Beloved has grown in (my) heart that (he) has merged (my) light in (his) light. Without water the chatrik cries out, Beloved, Beloved, and laments and wails; the thundering cloud rains in all ten directions, (but) without (the water it longs for, its) thirst does not go. The fish dwells (in water) and is born of water alone; (its) joy and sorrow are by its past deeds. It cannot live for an instant, the space of a sesame seed, a moment, without water; its death and life are with that (water). The bride is far away from home, the Husband dwells in (his own) land; she sends (him) a message by way of the true Guru. Gathering virtues, (she) makes God dwell in her heart; steeped in devotion, (she) rejoices. All, as many as there are, cry, Beloved, Beloved; (but she who) is pleasing to the Guru finds the Beloved. The Beloved is ever with (her), truly at (her) side; the Gracious One unites (her) in his union. In all is the soul, and that soul is he himself; he pervades every heart. By the Guru's grace (he) has shone forth in (her) very home, and (she) has merged, with ease, in Sahaj. O Master, Giver of peace, set right your own task yourself. By the Guru's grace (she) has found the Husband in (her) very home; then, O Nanak, (her) burning is quenched. ॥8॥
Ashtapadi (ashta, eight; pad, stanza): a hymn of about eight stanzas.
The chakvi (ruddy shelduck), parted from her mate at night, waits all night for the sunrise.
1273.3: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Through the Guru's service one stays awake and aware; without the Lord, no one is mine. For all one's efforts, none can stay (here); (bodies) melt away like glass in the heat. Tell me, what pride can there be in this body and wealth? They perish in no time, O madman; in this way the world wastes away in Haumai and pride. Hail to you, God, Lord of the world, the Protector; he alone saves and assays (all beings). All that is comes from you alone; there is none other equal to you. Creating beings, you have kept (their) way of life in your own control; you yourself (give) the eye-salve (of wisdom) through the Guru. My (Lord) is immortal, with no master, above the heads of all; he destroys death and birth, doubt and fear. This poor world is a fortress of paper, (decked) with colours, marks and cleverness; a tiny drop or a puff of wind destroys its glory; it is born and dies within an instant. As a house or a tree on the bank of a river, (or as) a she-serpent's lair inside a house, when the river turns, where are house and tree? The serpent strikes: (such is) duality in the mind. The Guru's wisdom, and meditation through the Guru's words, are the Garur; through the Guru's teaching (he) has burnt away (the poison of) Maya. (His) mind and body have grown cool as snow, (he) has found the True One; unique is devotion to the Lord. All that is begs of you; you are merciful to all beings. (We) have fallen at your refuge: keep (our) honour, O Gopal, that (we) may find the Truth. Bound in worldly affairs, (the world) is blind and does not see; it does the deeds of a hunter. If it meets the True Guru, then it sees and understands, and the wisdom of the True One settles in the mind. Without the Truth the body is without virtue and unripe; I ask my Guru. O Nanak, that (Guru, himself) God, shows God; without the True One the world is a dream. ॥9॥
1274.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The chatrik and the fish find peace in water alone; the deer delights in the sound (of the bell). O my mother, the rain-bird has called out in the night. Love for the Beloved never turns back, the love that pleases you. Sleep has gone, Haumai in the body is spent; the wisdom of Truth has settled in the heart. Flying from tree to tree and bush to bush, I go hungry; (now) I drink the Naam with love. (My) eyes are fixed in a steady gaze, (my) tongue cries out; (I) thirst for the sight of the Lord of the Will. Without the Beloved, the more I adorn myself, the more my body burns; clothes do not sit well on my limbs. Without my own Beloved I cannot stay for an instant; without meeting (him) I get no sleep. The Husband is near, but the poor (bride) does not understand; the True Guru has shown (him to her). When (he) was met in Sahaj, only then did (she) find peace; through the Shabad (her) craving was quenched. Says Nanak, through you, (O God,) (my) mind is content; (its) worth cannot be told. ॥10॥
Hunters draw the deer at night with the sound of a bell (ghanda hera); the deer gives up its life to that sound.
1274.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The crane flies high (in the sky), (but) the water is in the sea; the mountain is high, (but) the fort is in the depths below. Through reflection on the Guru's Shabad the (world-) ocean grows cool; killing Haumai, the path is opened. For me, the blind, the Name alone is the light; I walk by the support of the Name, in awe of the Guru, by (the Guru's) secret. (One who,) knowing the level road through the True Guru's Shabad, (walks) on the Guru's support, by the strength of the True One, (and) cherishes the Naam through the beautiful Bani, if it pleases you, (O God,) recognises (your) door and finds it. Whether I fly or sit, (my) mind's thread is fixed on the One; through the Guru's Shabad the Name is (my) support. (On my way) there is no water, no mountain, no high ridge; (I) dwell in my own home; there is no road there, and no one to walk it. (O God,) the home in which you dwell, you alone know its state; no other mansion is seen (by it). Without the True Guru understanding does not come; the whole world lies crushed under (Maya's) weight. (One) pleads piteously and wails, (but) without the Guru the Name is not known. If (one) recognises the Guru's Shabad, the Name sets (one) free in the blink of an eye. Some are fools, blind, witless and ignorant; some, in awe of the True Guru, lean on the Name. The true Bani is sweet, a stream of Amrit; whoever has drunk it (finds) the door of liberation. (Those who) enshrine the Naam in the heart with awe and love, (whose) deeds are the Guru's and (whose) word is Truth, (for them) Indra rains, the earth (of the heart) grows lovely, (and they see God's) light in every heart. (One of) evil mind sows in barren, salty soil: such is the mark of one without a Guru. Without the True Guru there is pitch darkness; (such people) have drowned and died without water. Whatever has been done is by God's will; what is written from the beginning cannot be erased; bound by (God's) Hukam, (each being) does its work. (One who) is absorbed in the Shabad of the One merges in the True One. O God, your Hukam prevails in the four directions; in the four directions and the netherworlds (is your) Name. In all, O God, (your) true Shabad is at work; by grace the Imperishable One is met. Birth and death are seen standing over (every) head, and hunger, sleep and death. O Nanak, (on whom falls) the true glance of grace of the Source of all delight, (he) receives the Naam, and it is pleasing to (his) mind. ॥8॥
1275.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (The soul-bird) does not know the worth of death, liberation and the higher state; sitting (only) on the bank, she (tries to) recognise (it) through the Guru's Shabad. O heron, how were you caught in the net? (For) you do not cherish the Unseen One in your heart and beg of him. For the sake of one life, you eat (many) lives; swimming in the water, (you) have drowned in that very water. You have tormented all creatures; when (you) were caught, only then did you repent. When a very heavy noose fell about (her) neck, (she) cannot spread her wings and fly. You peck (at the bait) with relish, O foolish manmukh; caught as you are, you are set free by reflecting on (God's) virtues and wisdom. By serving the True Guru, (the net of) Jamkaal is broken; cherish the true Shabad in your heart. The Guru's teaching is true; the Shabad is the essence; (through it, one) keeps the Name of the Lord enshrined in the heart. The pleasures and indulgences (of here) are sorrows ahead; O Nanak, without the true Name there is no liberation. ॥8॥
1276.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. If there is (God's) grace, the True Guru is found; without grace he cannot be found. Meeting the True Guru, one becomes gold, when it is the Lord's will. O my mind, fix your attention on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Through the True Guru the true Lord is found, and (one) remains merged in the Lord. From the True Guru wisdom springs up, and then this anxiety departs; from the True Guru the Lord is understood, and (one) does not fall into the womb and the species (again). By the Guru's grace one dies while alive, and, practising the Shabad, dies and lives (anew); he alone finds the door of liberation who sheds self-conceit from within. By the Guru's grace one is born in the house of Shiv, losing Shakti from within; (he) tames the untamable (mind), gains a discerning intellect, and the person is united with the Supreme Being. The world, a passing play, is heedless; (one) departs having lost the capital. The profit, the Lord, is found in the Sat Sangat; by grace it comes into (one's) hands. Without the True Guru no one has found (it): see for yourselves, reflecting in your mind and heart. The fortunate have found the Guru, and crossed over the world-ocean. The Lord's Name, the Lord himself, is (my) prop; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (my) support. Show grace, O dear Lord, unite (me) with the Guru, that I may find the door of liberation. What the Master has written on the brow from the beginning cannot be erased. O Nanak, perfect have become those to whom the Lord's will is pleasing. ॥8॥
1276.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The world goes by the word of the Vedas, and reflects on the three qualities; without the Name it bears the rod of Jam, and dies and is born again and again. Meeting the True Guru, one is set free, and finds the door of liberation. O mind, serve the True Guru and merge (in the Lord). (One who) has found the Perfect Guru by great good fortune meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. By his own will the Lord created the world; the Lord himself gives (it) support. By his own will the Lord has made (one's) mind pure, and love for the Lord has taken hold (of it). By the Lord's will (one) has met the True Guru, who sets right the whole of life. Waho Waho: the Bani of praise is true; rare is one who understands (it) through the Guru. Saying Waho Waho, one should praise God; there is none other as great as he. He himself forgives and unites (with himself); he is attained by grace. The true Master is supreme; the True Guru has shown (him). Amrit rains down, the mind is content, and (one) stays lovingly fixed on the True One. Through the Lord's Name (the soul) is ever green, and never again dries up or withers. Without the True Guru no one has found (him); let anyone satisfy himself, and see in his mind. Through the Lord's grace one finds the True Guru, and meets him with ease, of his own accord. The manmukh is led astray by doubt; without good fortune he does not obtain the wealth of the Lord. The three qualities are all Maya's wandering; (people) read and read and reflect on them. (They) are never set free, nor do they find the door of liberation. Without the True Guru the bonds do not break, and love for the Naam does not take hold. Pandits and silent sages have grown weary with reading and reading, and with study of the Vedas; the Lord's Name does not come to (their) minds, nor do (they) dwell in their own home. Jamkaal does not leave (their) heads; through the deceit within is (their) ruin. Everyone yearns for the Lord's Name, (but) without good fortune it cannot be found. (When he) casts his glance of grace, the Guru is met, and the Lord's Name comes to dwell in the mind. O Nanak, honour springs from the Name alone, and I remain merged in the Lord. ॥8॥
1277.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, an Ashtapadi, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (On whom) the Lord, Har Har, shows grace, (him) he sets to the Guru's work; taking away (his) pain, he makes the Lord's Name dwell (in him); (this is) the true state: he fixes (his) mind on the True One, (and) through the Shabad makes (him) hear the Bani of the Guru. O my mind, serve the Lord, Har Har: he is the treasure. By the Guru's grace the wealth of the Lord is found, and night and day the mind is fixed in Sahaj. If a woman adorns herself without her husband, she is called one of bad conduct, and is ever disgraced. Such is the manmukh's conduct, in vain: forgetting the Naam, (they) press (on others) many rites. The adornment of the Gurmukh bride is fitting; through the Shabad she has kept the Husband enshrined in her heart; killing Haumai, she recognises the One; that woman is called glorious. Without the Guru, the Giver, no one has found (him); the manmukh is lured by greed and duality. O wise ones, let anyone understand this: without meeting the Guru there is no liberation. Everyone talks and talks (of devotion); (but) without the mind dying, there is no devotion. With wisdom in the intellect the lotus (of the heart) blossoms; in that heart dwells the Naam, the Naam alone. Everyone performs devotion in Haumai; (so) the mind is not drenched (with love), nor is there peace. Talking and talking, (one) makes a show of oneself; (his) devotion is fruitless, and he wastes his whole life. Those devotees are pleasing to the True Guru's mind who stay lovingly fixed on the Naam night and day. They ever see the Naam present before them; through the Guru's Shabad, (he) is seen pervading everywhere. He himself forgives and gives (his) love; Haumai is a great disease in the world; by the Guru's grace this disease departs. O Nanak, (one) merges in the True One, in Truth itself. ॥8॥
1278.1: Raag Malar, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The Beloved is the Giver of love and devotion; he is dyed (in love) with his own servants. Dyed with his servants day and night, he does not slip from (their) minds for even an instant. Gopal, the treasure of virtues, is ever with (them); all virtues are in the Lord of the world. He has enchanted (their) minds with his feet; his servants are intoxicated with the relish of the Name. O Nanak, the Beloved is merciful for ever; among millions, (only) some rare one has known (him). O Beloved, your state is beyond reach and beyond limit; you have carried across even the greatest sinners. O Purifier of the fallen, Lover of devotion, O Master, Ocean of mercy! In the company of the Sants, worship (him) without reserve; ever remember the Knower of hearts. Those who wandered through the wombs for millions of births have been carried across by remembering the Name. Nanak thirsts for the sight of (you); O dear Lord, take (him) into your own care. (My) mind is merged in the Lord's lotus feet; O God, (you are) the water, and your servants are the fish. O dear God, the water and the fish are you alone; no other, apart (from you), is known. Take (me) by the arm, give (me) the Naam; by your grace (alone) is honour received. In the Saadh Sangat, with single-minded love, worship Gobind, merciful to the meek. Nanak, without a master and lowly, (came to) his refuge; showing mercy, (God) has made (him) his own. He has united his own self with himself, the Lord King, the Destroyer of doubt. The wondrous Master, the Knower of hearts, the treasure of virtues, has met (his) beloved ones; great joy and peace have welled up (in them); day after day (they) have cherished the virtues of Gobind. Meeting (him), they are made beautiful in (his) company; beholding (him), they are enraptured: they have received what was written (for them) before. Nanak prays: (I take) the refuge of those who have meditated on the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
Chhant: a song of longer stanzas.
1278.2: Malar ki Vaar: by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Rana Kailas and Malde. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When the Guru is met, the mind blossoms, as the earth is adorned when the rain has fallen; all (the land) looks green, and the lakes and pools are filled to the brim. The inner self is steeped in the love of the True One, like the deep red of madder; the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, the True One (dwells) in the mind, and through the Guru's Shabad (one is) delighted. The manmukh is on the other side: look and see with care. (He is) like a deer caught in a snare; Jamkaal is seen over (his) head. Hunger, craving, evil slander, lust and terrible anger (torment him); with these eyes (this state) is not seen, as long as (he) does not reflect through the Shabad. (O God,) when it pleases you, (these eyes) are contented, and the snare of household cares is ended. By serving the Guru the capital is kept safe; the Guru's ladder (is) the ship. O Nanak, she who holds fast (to it) obtains the essence; (O Lord,) you, the True One, (dwell) in (her) mind for ever. ॥1॥

A vaar is a hymn of pauris (stanzas); the pauris of this vaar are the First Guru's (one of them the Fifth Guru's), and each is preceded by saloks of the First, Second, Third and Fifth Gurus. Rana Kailas and Malde: by tradition, Kailas Dev and Mal Dev, two brothers who ruled in Jammu and Kashmir, whose fight the bards sang as a vaar; this vaar is to be sung to its tune (dhuni).
1279.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). There is one level road, one door; by the Guru's ladder (one reaches one's) own true place. O Nanak, the Master is beautiful; all comforts lie in the true Name. ॥2॥
1279.2: He himself fashioned himself, and recognised himself. Parting the sky from the earth, he has stretched out (the sky as) a canopy. Holding up the heavens without pillars, he has made (his) Word (his Hukam) the sign (of his rule). Creating the sun and the moon, he has set (his) light in them. He has made night and day, (his) wondrous plays. Pilgrimages, religious duties, reflection, and bathing at the holy festivals (are of his making too). (O God,) none other is equal to you: what can be said to describe (you)? (Your) dwelling is on the true throne; all others come and go. ॥1॥
1279.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, if it rains in Sawan, four are filled with joy: snakes, deer, fish, and the lovers of pleasure who have wealth at home. ॥1॥
1279.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, if it rains in Sawan, four suffer separation: the oxen (the sons of cows), the poor, the wayfarer, and the one who is a servant. ॥2॥
1279.5: You are the True One, the Master of truth, who has made the truth prevail. You sat in deep absorption (in yourself), the lotus (of creation) (still) kept hidden; Brahma, calling himself great, did not find (your) end. He has no father, no mother: who gave birth to you? He has no form, no outline; all colours (are his). He has no hunger, no thirst; (he is ever) filled and content. Merging himself in the Guru, he has spread the Shabad abroad. (One who is) content in the True One alone merges in the True One. ॥2॥
In the Puranas Brahma was born of a lotus that grew from Vishnu's navel, and went down its stalk to find where it began, but found no end.
1279.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The physician was called in to give treatment; he takes the arm and feels (for the pulse). The simple physician does not know that the ache is in the heart. ॥1॥
1279.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). O physician, you are a physician, a skilled physician: first recognise the disease; seek out such a medicine as will rid (one) of the whole heap of diseases, the medicine by which diseases are lifted, and peace comes to dwell in the body. Says Nanak, if you rid yourself of your own disease, then call yourself a physician. ॥2॥
1279.8: He created the gods Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh (Shiva). To Brahma he gave the Vedas, and set (him) to worship. Among the ten avatars came Ram the king; rushing (on them), he slew the demons: all of it by (God's) Hukam. Isa and Mahesar (Shiva in his forms) served (him), (but) they did not find his end. Setting (on it his) true worth, he has fashioned (his) throne; setting the world to its tasks, he has hidden himself. Dharam (righteousness) has (beings) do their deeds: so (he) has commanded from the source. ॥3॥
1280.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Sawan has come, O friend: keep the Husband in your hearts. O Nanak, the forsaken brides, who have fallen in love with others, pine away and die. ॥1॥
1280.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Sawan has come, O friend; the cloud is about to rain. O Nanak, let the happy wives who love their Husband sleep in peace. ॥2॥
1280.3: He himself has set the wrestling match going and made the arena. (The wrestlers) have come down (into it) with a clamour; the Gurmukh is in full vigour. The manmukhs, the foolish weaklings, he has thrown down and beaten. He himself wrestles, he himself strikes down; he himself has staged the event. The One is the Master of all; through the Guru he is known. By his Hukam he writes the destiny on (each) head, without pen or inkpot. Union (with him comes) in the Sat Sangat, where the Lord's praises are ever told. O Nanak, praising the true Shabad, one recognises the True One. ॥4॥
1280.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Bending low and lower, (the cloud) has come, showing many colours. What do I know of how (my) love for that King will last? Love has lasted for those brides in whose minds are awe and love. O Nanak, those without awe and love find no peace in their bodies. ॥1॥
1280.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Bending low and lower, (the cloud) has come; clear water rains down. O Nanak, pain clings to those brides whose minds are broken off from the Husband. ॥2॥
1280.6: Creating both sides, the One pervades (them). Spreading the word of the Vedas, he has put strife within (them). Pravirti and nirvirti (involvement in the world and withdrawal from it) are the two sides; between them Dharam goes about as the guide. The manmukhs are unripe and false; they have surely lost (the game) in the Lord's court. Those who follow the Guru's teaching are heroes through the Shabad, who have killed lust and anger.
