Within the mansion of the True One, they are adorned through the Shabad. Those devotees are pleasing to you, (O God,) who are in love with the true Name. Those who serve their own True Guru: to them I am a sacrifice. ॥5॥
1280.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Bending low and lower, (the cloud) has come; it rains in a steady downpour. O Nanak, she who walks in her Husband's will enjoys delight for ever. ॥1॥
1280.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Why do you rise again and again to look, poor wretches? Nothing is in this cloud's hands. Keep in your minds the One who has sent this cloud. He alone will enshrine him in (his) mind, on whom (the Lord) casts (his) glance of grace. O Nanak, without (his) glance of grace, all (the world) pleads and laments. ॥2॥
1280.9: One should ever serve that Lord who takes no time to create. Having made the outspread skies, he can tear down and build up again in an instant. Having created the world himself, he reflects on his creation. Hereafter the manmukh is called to account, and is beaten hard. The Gurmukh's account is settled with honour; (the Lord) bestows on (him) treasures of praise. There no hand can reach, and no cry or wail is heard. There the True Guru is the friend, and at the very last he pulls (one) out. For these beings there is no other service (of worth); over (their) heads is the True Guru, the Creator. ॥6॥
1281.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O rain-bird, the One you call out for, everyone longs for. Showing his own grace he will rain, and forest and grass turn green. By the Guru's grace (he) is found; some rare one understands (this). Sitting and standing, one should meditate (on him) day after day; (then) there is peace for ever and ever. O Nanak, Amrit ever rains down; through the Guru that Lord gives (it). ॥1॥
1281.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The earth has grown distressed, and prays with (its) mind fixed (on him); the True One listened, giving ear, and gives comfort with ease, of his own accord. He commanded Indra, and (he) rained in torrents. The wealth of grain springs up in great abundance; its worth cannot be told. O Nanak, praise the Name (of the One) who gives all beings their sustenance, bringing it to them, eating which, peace wells up, and pain does not come to touch (one) again. ॥2॥
1281.3: O dear Lord, you are true, truly true; the true you unite (with yourself). In duality (one) is on the other side; through falsehood (he) is not met, he cannot be met. He himself joins the one (he has) parted; he himself displays (his) creative power. (For the false) there is attachment, sorrow and separation; (he) acts out what was written before. I am a sacrifice to those who keep their minds fixed on the Lord's feet; as the lotus in the water stays untouched, such is the way (the Lord) has made (for them). They are at peace and ever beautiful, who have shed self-conceit from within. They never know sorrow or separation, who are absorbed in the Lord's embrace. ॥7॥
1281.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O Nanak, one should praise him in whose power everything lies. Serve him alone, O mortals; without him there is no other. (When) through the Guru the Lord God dwells in the mind, then there is peace for ever and ever. There is no dread at all, and all anxiety goes from within. Whatever happens, happens in Sahaj; nothing at all can be said (against it). (When) the true Master dwells in the mind, then (one) obtains the fruit the mind longs for. O Nanak, he himself listens to the words of those whom he has entered on his own page. ॥1॥
1281.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Amrit rains for ever; those able to understand understand (this). Those who have understood through the Guru keep the Lord's Amrit enshrined in their hearts. They drink the Lord's Amrit for ever, dyed in (his) love, having killed Haumai and craving. Amrit is the Name of the Lord, which rains down by (his) grace. O Nanak, through the Guru the Lord has come into view, the all-pervading Ram (Atam Ram), Murari. ॥2॥
1282.1: How can the Unweighable be weighed? (Yet) unless he is weighed, he cannot be found. Through the Guru's Shabad one should reflect (on him); (so one) stays absorbed in (his) virtues. He himself will weigh his own self; he himself brings about the union in which he is met. His worth cannot be reckoned; nothing at all can be said (of him). I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has given (me) true understanding. The world is being cheated, its Amrit plundered, (but) the manmukh does not grasp (this). Without the Name, nothing will accompany (him); he will depart, having wasted his life. Those who are awake through the Guru's teaching have kept their house safe; the demons (the five enemies) have no power (over them). ॥8॥
1282.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O rain-bird, do not wail, do not make this mind pine; obey the Master's Hukam. O Nanak, by obeying the Hukam thirst is quenched, and the colour (of love) deepens fourfold. ॥1॥
1282.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O rain-bird, your dwelling is in the water; in the water itself you move about; (yet) you do not know the worth of the water, and so you cry out. On sea and land, in all four directions, it rains; no place is left empty. With so much water raining down, those who die of thirst have no good fortune. O Nanak, through the Guru understanding has come to those in whose minds (the Lord) has come to dwell. ॥2॥
1282.4: Naths, celibates, Siddhas and Pirs: none has found (your) end. Meditating on the Naam through the Guru, (one) has merged in you. For thirty-six ages there was pitch darkness: so it pleased him. He it was who spread out the fearsome expanse of the waters. Beyond all count, beyond reach, the Ever-living is (himself) all. He created fire, strife, hunger and thirst. Death hangs over the head of the world, (for) duality has pleased it. The Saviour, who has given (one) understanding of the Shabad, keeps (him) safe. ॥9॥
The Naths: the perfected masters of the yogis, such as Gorakhnath. The Siddhas are yogis held to have reached perfection.
1282.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). This water rains everywhere; it rains with love, as (he) wills. Those trees (alone) are green which, through the Guru, stay absorbed (in it). O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace there is peace, and the pain of these beings departs. ॥1॥
1282.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In the dew-wet night (the cloud) flashed, and rained in torrents; by its raining the wealth of grain springs up in plenty, when the Husband Lord so wills; eating which the mind is satisfied, and the way of life comes into (all) beings. This wealth is the Creator's play: sometimes it comes, sometimes it goes. The wealth of those who know (God) is the Naam; it abides (in them) for ever. O Nanak, those on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace: then he places this wealth in their laps. ॥2॥
1282.7: He himself causes and he himself does; to whom am I to complain? He himself will call (all) to account; he himself has (them) do (their) work. Whatever pleases him, that comes to pass; the fool (only) gives orders. If he himself sets one free, one is freed; he himself is the Forgiver. He himself sees, he himself hears; he gives support to all. The One pervades all; he takes thought for each and every one. Through the Guru one should reflect on one's own self; (then) love for the True One takes hold. O Nanak, to whom is one to speak? (The Lord) himself is the Giver. ॥10॥
1283.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The rain-bird is this world; let no one be led astray by doubt. This rain-bird is a beast; it has no understanding. Amrit is the Name of the Lord, which, when drunk, takes thirst away. O Nanak, those who have drunk it through the Guru: (thirst) has not come to cling to them again. ॥1॥
1283.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Malar is a cooling raag; by meditating on the Lord there is peace. When the dear Lord shows his own grace, then (the rain) falls over all the world. When it has rained, beings find the way of life, and the earth is adorned. O Nanak, this whole world is water; from water alone is every one (born). By the Guru's grace some rare one understands (this); that person is free for ever. ॥2॥
1283.3: You alone are the Master, true and free of all want. You yourself are everything: whom else should I count? Man's pride is false; your greatness is true. Making coming and going, you created the world. One who serves his own True Guru: his coming (into the world) I count (as fruitful). If Haumai goes from within, then what account is (left) to be reckoned? The manmukh (wanders) in the darkness of attachment, like one lost in the forest. Countless sins are cut away by a single particle of the Name. ॥11॥
1283.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O rain-bird, you do not know the Master's mansion; look upon the mansion and offer (your) prayer. You speak a great deal by your own will; (such) speech is not accepted. The Master is a great Giver; whatever (one) wishes for, that fruit (one) obtains. What of the poor rain-bird alone? The thirst of the (whole) world departs. ॥1॥
1283.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The rain-bird has called out in the dew-wet night, in Sahaj, (absorbed) in the True One, with love: This water is my life; without water I cannot live. Through the Guru's Shabad the water is found, by shedding self-conceit from within. O Nanak, the One without whom (the soul) cannot live a moment, the True Guru has brought (her) to meet. ॥2॥
1283.6: The worlds and netherworlds are countless; I cannot count them. You are the Creator, Govind; you created (it), and you yourself destroy (it). The eighty-four lakh forms of life on earth have come from you alone. Some call themselves kings, khans and lords, and have others call them so. Some, hoarding wealth, are called bankers; in duality they have lost (their) honour. Some are givers, some beggars; over the heads of all is he alone. Without the Name they are (mere) showmen, and (the earth) is in dread (of them). O Nanak, the false (wares) run out; what the True One does, that comes to be. ॥12॥
1283.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O rain-bird, the virtuous (bride) has reached the mansion; the one full of faults is far away. Within you the Lord dwells; through the Guru (he is seen) ever present. (Then) there is no crying out or wailing; by the glance of the Gracious One (one is) delighted. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam meet (him) in Sahaj, by toiling in the Guru's Shabad. ॥1॥
1284.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The rain-bird prays: (O God,) show grace and give (me) the gift of life. Without water (my) thirst is not quenched; my breath is slipping away. You are the Giver of peace, the Infinite, the Giver of virtues, the Treasure. O Nanak, through the Guru (the Lord) forgives (one), and in the end God becomes (his) friend. ॥2॥
1284.2: Having created the world himself, he reflects on (its) virtues and faults. The three qualities are nothing but entanglement; (caught in them, one) does not set (one's) love on the Naam. (Those who,) leaving virtues, practise faults are disgraced in the Lord's court. They have lost their life in a gamble: why did they come into the world? Those who have subdued the mind by the true Shabad, (and abide) day and night in the Naam, in love, those men who have enshrined in their hearts the True One, the Unseen, the Infinite, (pray thus): You are the Giver of virtues, the Treasure; we are full of faults. He whom (God) forgives will obtain (this) reflection through the Guru's Shabad. ॥13॥
1284.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The night does not pass for the Saakats, who forget the Name. Nights and days pass in comfort, O Nanak, singing the praises of the Lord. ॥1॥
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
1284.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Jewels, gems and rubies, all precious stones, (shine) on the foreheads of those, O Nanak, who are pleasing to God; they look beautiful at the true door. ॥2॥
1284.5: (Those who,) serving the True Guru, the true one, have cherished the True One: what (they) toiled for before the True Guru has come to stand by (them) at the end. Jamkaal cannot touch (them); the True One is (their) protector. Kindling the light of the Guru's teaching, (they) have lit the lamp (within). The manmukhs, without the Name, are false; they wander about out of step. They are beasts wrapped in human skin, black within. The True One pervades all; through the true Shabad (he) is beheld. O Nanak, the Naam is a treasure, (which) the Perfect Guru has shown. ॥14॥
1284.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The rain-bird has recognised the Hukam, in the Sahaj given by the Guru, with love. The cloud rains in mercy, in heavy torrents. The rain-bird's crying out and wailing have ceased; peace has come to dwell in (its) mind. O Nanak, one should praise him who gives all beings their sustenance, bringing it to them. ॥1॥
1284.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O chatrik, you do not know what thirst is in you, (nor) by drinking what the thirst will go. Wandering in the love of another, (you) do not obtain the Amrit water. If (God) casts his own glance of grace, then the True Guru is met, as a matter of course. O Nanak, (one who) has received the Amrit water from the True Guru stays absorbed in Sahaj. ॥2॥
1284.8: Some go and sit in the forests, and do not utter a word. Some break through frost and ice to endure icy water. Some smear ashes on their bodies, and never wash away the grime. Some, with matted hair, tangled and fearsome, lose their family and home. Some go about naked day and night, and do not sleep. Some burn their bodies in fire, and ruin themselves. Without the Name the body (turns to) ash: what can they say as they weep? They look beautiful at the Master's door, who serve the True Guru. ॥15॥
1285.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When the rain-bird called out in the Amrit vela (the hours before daybreak), (its) cry was heard at the (Lord's) door. The command went to the cloud: show mercy and pour down rain. I am a sacrifice to those who have kept the True One fixed in the heart. O Nanak, through the Name all (the world) turns green, by reflection on the Guru's Shabad. ॥1॥
1285.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O rain-bird, your thirst is not quenched this way, even if you cry out a hundred times. By (God's) glance of grace the True Guru is found; by (his) glance of grace love wells up. O Nanak, (when) the Master dwells in the mind, the vices depart from within. ॥2॥
1285.3: Some, the Jains, (the Lord) has set on a wild path and led astray from the very start. The Name is not in their mouths, nor do they bathe at a place of pilgrimage. They have the hair of their heads plucked out by hand, and do not have their heads shaved. They stay filthy day and night; the Shabad does not please them. They have no caste, no honour, no (good) deeds; they have wasted their lives. Impure in mind, these men of no caste eat (others') leavings. Without the Shabad, no one has attained good conduct. The Gurmukh stays merged in Oankar, the True One. ॥16॥
This pauri is about the Jain monks of the time, who, for fear of harming the smallest living being, had their hair plucked out, and neither bathed nor drank fresh water.
1285.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Sawan the bride, reflecting through the Guru's Shabad, flourishes, full of delight. O Nanak, through boundless love for the Guru, she is ever a happy wife. ॥1॥
1285.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Sawan she burns who is without virtue, whose love is caught in the love of another. O Nanak, she does not know the worth of her Husband; all her adornment only brings her to ruin. ॥2॥
1285.6: The True One, unseen and unfathomable, is not won over by stubborn effort (hath). Some sing the raags and raginis, (but) he is not moved by raag. Some dance and dance to keep the beat, (but) devotion is not done (this way). Some fools do not eat grain: what can be done with them? Craving has grown great, and is calmed in no way. Rites multiply among many peoples; (in them) one wastes away and dies. The Name is the profit in the world; one should drink the Amrit (of the Name). The Gurmukh is drenched in devotion to the Lord and in love (for him). ॥17॥
1285.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who sing Raag Malar through the Guru: their mind and body grow cool. Through the Guru's Shabad they have recognised the One, the one and only True One. (Their) mind and body are true, the True One (dwells) in (their) mind; true is the renown of those true ones. Within (them) is true devotion; in Sahaj they are honoured. In Kalyug there is pitch darkness; the manmukhs have no way (out). Fortunate are they, O Nanak, in whom (the Lord) is revealed through the Guru. ॥1॥
1285.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (When) Indra rains in mercy, joy wells up in people's minds. I am ever a sacrifice to him by whose Hukam Indra rains. Through the Guru one should cherish the Shabad; I sing the virtues of the True One. O Nanak, the servants (of the Lord) dyed in the Name are pure; in Sahaj they are absorbed in the True One. ॥2॥
1286.1: Serving the Perfect True Guru, (he) has found the Perfect One. By perfect grace, meditating (on God), (he) has enshrined the perfect Shabad in (his) mind. Through perfect wisdom and meditation, (he) has washed away the filth (of the mind). Knowing the Lord as the pool, the place of pilgrimage, (his) mind has bathed (in him). He who dies through the Shabad, subduing the mind: blessed is the mother who bore him. At the true door he is (held) true; true is his coming (into the world). No one can call (him) to account, since he is pleasing to the Master. O Nanak, praising the True One, (he) has received what was written (for him). ॥18॥
1286.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Foolish are those who give caps (kulah); those who take them are utterly shameless. The mouse cannot fit into its hole, and yet it ties a winnowing basket to its waist. Those who give blessings die, and those to whom they give them depart (as well). O Nanak, (God's) Hukam is not known: where (they) go and merge. The one Name is (my) crop of Harh, the true Name (my) crop of Sawan. Going to the Master's door, I have had the title-deed (to it) written out. The doors of the world are so many; so many come and go (at them). So many beggars beg, so many go away having begged and begged. ॥1॥
Kulah: the cap a pir gave a disciple when he made him his successor. Aharhi is the crop reaped in the month of Harh, Sawani the crop sown in Sawan.
1286.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The elephant eats a hundred maunds of ghee and gur, and eats five hundred (maunds) of grain; it belches, it snorts, it scatters dust; when the breath has gone, it is sorry. The blind and crazed (world) has died puffing itself up in pride. Only when effaced in the Master is she then pleasing (to him). Half a grain is the sparrow's feed; it rises into the sky and chirps. That (sparrow) pleases the Master, she is good, who calls out, Khuda, Khuda (God, God). The mighty lion kills hundreds of deer, and all (the other beasts) follow behind him and eat. Grown strong, he cannot fit into his den; when the breath has gone, he is sorry. To whom does the blind one roar out his boasts? He is not pleasing to the Master at all. The insect of the ak (the milkweed) loves the ak; it sits on the ak's branch and eats (it). That (insect) pleases the Master, it is good, which calls out, Khuda, Khuda. O Nanak, the world (lasts but) four days; pleasures enjoyed turn to pain. There are many who talk (of it), (but) no one can let it go. Flies die on sweetness. Those whom you protect, (O Lord,) it does not come near; they are to cross the ocean of fear. ॥2॥
1286.4: You are beyond reach, beyond the grasp of the senses, the Master; (you are) the True One, unseen and infinite. You are the Giver, all are beggars; you alone are the One who gives. Those who have served (you) have found peace, and understanding through the Guru's teaching. For some, this is what pleases you: that (their) love is for Maya. Through the Guru's Shabad one should praise (you), with love and affection within. Devotion does not come about without love; without the True Guru, love is not kindled. You are God, and all serve you; (your) minstrel makes one plea: give (me) the gift that (I) may be content, and that the true Name may be given (me) as (my) support. ॥19॥
1287.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With the nights (life's) time wanes, with the days (life's) time (wanes); the body wears away and becomes (like) straw. (Worldly) dealings have spread over all as an entanglement; gone astray, (man) has lost the measure of austerity (the way of devotion). The blind one, flailing about again and again, has fallen into the wrangle (of the world). Afterwards (his kin) weep, (wishing to) bring (him) back. Without understanding, nothing is clear (to them). They weep for the dead, and weeping, (they themselves) die. O Nanak, so it pleases the Master. They alone are dead, in whose minds (the Lord) does not come. ॥1॥
1287.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Love has died, affection has died, and the quarrelsome enmity has died. The colour has gone, the beauty has perished; the poor body lies in the dust. Where did (he) come from, where has he gone? What was he not, what was he? (He) spoke words in (his) mind and with (his) mouth, and made merry and revelled. O Nanak, without the True Name, (his) honour is in tatters from head to foot. ॥2॥
1287.3: The Amrit Name is ever the Giver of peace; at the end it becomes (one's) companion. Without the Guru the world has gone mad; it has not grasped the Name's worth. Those who serve the True Guru are accepted, who have merged (their) light in the Light. As that Master is, so becomes the servant in whose mind (the Master) settles his will. Say, who has found peace by his own will? The blind one does only blind deeds. (He) is never satisfied with the poison (of Maya); the fool's hunger does not go. Attached to another, everyone is ruined; without the True Guru, understanding is not gained. He serves the True Guru and finds peace, on whom the Lord of the Will shows grace. ॥20॥
1287.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Honour and righteousness, both, O Nanak, (are held to come) if wealth falls into one's lap. One should not call that wealth a friend, for whose sake (one) takes blows on the head. Those who have wealth in their lap: their name is beggar. (O Lord,) those in whose hearts you dwell are men deep as the ocean in virtue. ॥1॥
1287.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Worldly wealth is gathered through pains, and when it goes, pains strike. O Nanak, no one's hunger has been removed without the True Name. Hunger does not leave by (gazing on) beauty; whenever I look, (there is more) hunger. However many the body's pleasures, so many are the pains that strike. ॥2॥
1287.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Through blind deeds the mind is blind; with the mind blind, the body is blind. What use is plastering with mud, when the dam of stones gives way? The dam is broken; no boat is there, no raft, and no (finding) the depth. O Nanak, without the True Name, how many caravans have drowned! ॥3॥
1287.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Lakhs of maunds of gold, lakhs of maunds of silver, a rich man above lakhs of rich men; lakhs of armies, lakhs of drums and spears, kings of lakhs of horses; (but) where the ocean is to be crossed, fire and water beyond all depth, (where) no shore comes into sight, and an uproar of wailing rises: there, O Nanak, it is known which are the rich and which the kings. ॥4॥
1287.8: Some have chains on their necks, (held) in God's prison. The bound are freed through the Truth, (when) the True One is recognised. (When) what is written comes into one's lap, (then) that True One is known. By (God's) Hukam the judgement is made; (this) is known (when one) has gone (from here). Through the Shabad one should recognise the One who carries (beings) across the fearsome world-ocean. Thieves, adulterers and gamblers are crushed (like seed) in the oil press. Slanderers and the untrustworthy (laitbar) are locked in the stocks. The Gurmukh who merges in the True One is known in the Lord's court. ॥21॥
1288.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The beggar is named king, the fool is named pandit (scholar); the blind man is named a judge of worth: such is the talk (of the world). The mischief-maker is named chaudhri (headman), and the false woman takes the foremost place. O Nanak, through the Guru it is understood: this is the justice of Kalyug. ॥1॥
1288.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Deer, hawks and officials: these are named the learned (the trained); with the snare set, they trap their own kind; hereafter they have no place. He is learned, he is a pandit and wise, who has practised the Name. First the root takes hold within (the ground), (and) then there is shade above. The kings are lions, the headmen dogs; they go and rouse (people) sitting or asleep; the servants (of the kings) wound (them) with their claws: O dogs, go on, lick up (their) blood and bile. (But) where beings will be judged, (there) the untrustworthy will have their noses cut off. ॥2॥
1288.3: He himself creates the earth, and he himself looks after it. Without the fear (of God) doubt is not cut away, nor does love for the Name take hold. The fear (of God) wells up from the True Guru; (by it) the door of liberation is found. Through the fear (of God) Sahaj is found, (one's) light merging in the infinite Light. Through the fear (of God) one gets across the fearsome world-ocean, reflecting through the Guru's teaching. Through the fear (of God) the Fearless One is found, who has no end, no near shore or far. The manmukhs do not know the worth of the fear (of God); burning in craving, they cry out. O Nanak, through the Name alone is peace found, holding (it) in the heart through the Guru's teaching. ॥22॥
1288.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Beauty and lust are friends; hunger and taste are tied together. Greed and wealth are blended into one; to the drowsy, a cramped corner is a bed. Anger barks; ruined, the blind (man) spouts empty abuse. O Nanak, silence is better; without the Name the mouth holds only a stench. ॥1॥
1288.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Power, wealth, beauty, caste and youth: all five are cheats. These cheats have cheated the world; no one has saved his honour. These (cheats) are themselves cheated by those who throw themselves at the Guru's feet. O Nanak, so many others, without (his) grace, are being plundered. ॥2॥
1288.6: The learned man is answerable; (his) account is called for. Without the Name he is false, and is hard pressed and distressed. (His) ways are hard and blocked, the lanes shut off. The True One, free of all need, (is met) through the Shabad by the contented. He is deep, profound and fathomless; his depth is not found. (You) take blow upon blow on the face; without the Guru no one will be freed. Go home with honour: one should utter the Name. One should know (him) as the One who, by (his) Hukam, gives breath and food. ॥23॥
1289.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Living beings are (made) of air, water and fire; what joys and what pains are theirs! (Some are) on the earth, (some) in the nether regions, (some) in the skies; some stay at court as ministers. Some have long lives; some die and are left in distress. Some give and eat, and (their store) does not run out; some go about as beggars all their lives. By (his) Hukam he creates, by (his) Hukam he pulls down lakhs in a single instant. Everyone is held by (his) nose-rope; (whom) he forgives, (his) rope he breaks. He is beyond colours and marks, beyond (all) reckoning, unseen. How can (he) be described, how spoken of? He is seen to be the True One, truth itself. O Nanak, all doing and speaking is (his) appointed work; he himself is beyond telling. (Whoever) hears the story of the Indescribable gains riddhis (wealth), wisdom, siddhis (miraculous powers), knowledge, and peace for ever. ॥1॥
1289.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If one endures the unendurable, the nine openings (of the body) are held in check; (if) one worships (the Lord) with each breath, the body grows steady. (Then) where has this one come from, where is he to go? Remaining dead while alive, he is accepted. He understands the Hukam and recognises the essence; this grace he knows (to come) from the Guru. O Nanak, know: he who asserts that he is will be seized; (where) there is no I and no me, (there is no) falling into births. ॥2॥
1289.3: One should read the Name and (the Lord's) praise; other learning is false. Without the true trade, life is in vain. No one has found (his) end, or his near and far shore. The whole world is in the darkness of pride; the Truth has not pleased them. Those who depart forgetting the Name are fried in the pan. Double-mindedness has poured oil into the blaze. (Such a one) comes, the play breaks up, and he wanders astray. O Nanak, those dyed in the True One are united with the True One. ॥24॥
1289.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). First (man) was conceived in flesh, and dwelt within flesh. When life was put in (him), flesh was given him in the mouth; bone, skin and body are flesh. Brought out of the flesh, (he had) flesh, the breast, for (his) food. The mouth is of flesh, the tongue of flesh; the breath is within flesh. He grew up and was married, and brought flesh home. From flesh alone flesh is born; all kinship comes from flesh. When the True Guru is met, the Hukam is understood; then one comes out right. By breaking free on one's own, one is not freed; O Nanak, in (mere) talk is ruin. ॥1॥
1289.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The fool quarrels over meat, crying meat, and knows nothing of wisdom and meditation. What is called meat, and what greens? In which of them is sin contained? Killing the rhinoceros, they made burnt offerings and sacrifices, as was the way of the gods. Giving up meat, they sit holding their noses, (but) at night they devour men. They put on a show for people to see; they have no sense of wisdom or meditation. O Nanak, what can be said to the blind? (If one) says (it), he does not understand what is said. He alone is blind whose deeds are blind; in his heart are no such eyes. Formed from the blood of mother and father, (yet) they do not eat fish or meat. When woman and man meet at night, there too it is with flesh that they consort. Of flesh we were conceived, of flesh we were born; we are vessels of flesh. He has no grasp at all of wisdom and meditation, (yet) the pandit calls himself clever. Flesh from outside is bad, sir, and the flesh of the home is better? All beings and creatures have come from flesh; the life (in them) has made its dwelling (in flesh). What is not to be eaten they eat, and what may be eaten they forsake, those whose guru is blind. Of flesh we were conceived, of flesh we were born; we are vessels of flesh. He has no grasp at all of wisdom and meditation, (yet) the pandit calls himself clever. Meat is in the Puranas, meat in the Kateb (the Semitic scriptures); through all four ages meat has been in use. At sacrifices, festivities and weddings it is thought fitting; meat has its place there. Women and men, kings and sultans, are born of flesh. If they are seen to be going to hell, then their gifts should not be taken. The giver to hell, the takers to heaven: look at this outrage! He does not understand himself, (yet) he instructs the people: the pandit is very wise indeed! O pandit, you do not even know where flesh has come from. From water come grain, sugarcane and cotton; from water the three worlds are reckoned (to arise). Water says: I do good in many ways; in water are many transformations. Let one give up all these relishes and become a sannyasi (a renunciant): so Nanak says, having reflected. ॥2॥
1290.1: What can I say with one tongue? No one has found your end. Those who reflect on the true Shabad merge in you alone. Some wander in saffron robes; without the True Guru no one has found (you). They have grown weary roaming land after land, (but) you have hidden yourself within (them). The Guru's Shabad is a jewel; kindling the light, (you) yourself have revealed (yourself). (He who) has recognised his own self has merged, through the Guru's teaching, in the True One. Coming and going is (the lot) of the showmen who have set up a market (of display). Those whose minds the True One pleases praise the One, the abiding True One. ॥25॥
1290.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, the tree of Maya, (grown) from deeds, (bears) fruits of Amrit and fruits of poison. The Creator makes all the causes; whom he feeds (a fruit), that one (eats it). ॥1॥
1290.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). O Nanak, burn the glories of the world in the fire. These wretched things have made (man) forget the Name; not one of them has gone along (with anyone). ॥2॥
1290.4: Each one's account is settled for each; (you) have set (all) going by (your) Hukam. The judgement is in your hands; you alone are dear to (my) mind. Death binds (one) and drives (him) on; no one will (be able to) keep (him). Old age, the tyrant, will dance, mounted on (one's) shoulders. The True Guru is the ship and the boat; the True One will save (one). The fire roars in a blaze, and will blaze night and day. Trapped, (the bird) pecks at the feed; by (God's) Hukam alone will it be freed. What the Creator does, that will be; falsehood will run out. ॥26॥
1291.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). He who shows the home within the home (of the heart) is the True Guru, the wise Being. There the five Shabads (sounds) ring in an unbroken strain, and the Shabad beats like a kettledrum. There (one sees) continents, worlds, nether regions, realms and spheres, and is wonderstruck. There instruments sound high and thunderous, (and) the King (sits) on the true throne. Hearing the music in the home of Sukhmana, (one) fixes (one's) attention in the realm of Sunn (stillness). (There) the story of the Indescribable is reflected on, and the mind's desire is absorbed in the mind itself. The lotus (of the heart) has turned over and is filled with Amrit; this mind goes nowhere (else). The ajapa jap is not forgotten; (the mind) merges in (him who is) from the beginning, from before the ages. All the companions (the senses) and the five (virtues) have met; through the Guru (one) dwells in (one's) own true home. One who searches out the Shabad and finds this home: Nanak is his servant. ॥1॥

Sukhmana: in the yogis' teaching, the central channel of the subtle body, said to open in the highest bliss. The five Shabads: the music of the five kinds of instrument (strings, metal, wind, skin drums and pots). Ajapa jap: remembrance that goes on unbroken, without repeating with the tongue.
1291.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The world is a great flash of lightning, passing away. I, a mere shell of wit, did not keep the grave in mind. I am base, the lowest of the low; O God, you are the river (of bounty). Give me the one thing (your Name); other things are poison, they do not please (me). (This body is) an unbaked cup filled with water, (made) by your craft, O God. You are mighty; I have come (into the world) by your power. Nanak, the dog of (your) court, is intoxicated; may (this intoxication) grow day by day. The world is fire, O God; cool is (your) Name. ॥2॥

This salok is in Persian words: chilimili (a flash of lightning), bisiar (much), fani (passing away), kalub (a mould, a frame), man (I), gor (the grave), kamin (base), kamtarin (the lowest), purab (full of water), kham (unbaked), kuza (a cup), hikmat (craft), tuana (mighty), sag (dog), diban (court), atas (fire), khunak (cool).
1291.3: A new pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). All that goes on is (his) play; it is told as a play. Paarbrahm, the Supreme God, is known through the Guru. All vices have been cast off through the Shabad, the beating drum. In the Saadh's company is deliverance; they have become free of want. Remembering the Giver again and again, they have enjoyed all delights. (The one who remembers) has become manifest in the world, with (God's) grace over (him) as a canopy. He himself forgives and unites (with himself); (I am) ever a sacrifice (to him). O Nanak, those who please the Master he unites (with himself). ॥27॥
1291.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Blessed is that paper, blessed the pen, blessed the inkpot and blessed the ink; blessed, O Nanak, is the writer who has had the True Name written. ॥1॥
1291.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord,) you yourself are the tablet, you yourself the pen, and the writing upon it too is you. O Nanak, one should speak of the One alone; why (speak of) a second? ॥2॥
1291.6: You yourself are at work (in all), and you yourself have shaped the design (of the world). There is no other without you; you pervade (all). Your state and your measure you alone know; you alone have set your worth. You are unseen, beyond the senses, beyond reach; the Guru's teaching has given the sight (of you). Within (a being) are ignorance, pain and doubt; the Guru's wisdom has driven (them) out. Whom you show grace, you unite (with yourself); that one meditates on the Naam. You are the Creator, the Being beyond reach, pervading every place. Whatever task you set (a being) to, O True One, to that he applies himself; Nanak sings (your) praises.
Sudh (corrected): written after the closing numbers of the vaar, it marks that the text was checked against the original.
1292.1: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I have served Gopal, the King, who has no lineage, the Immaculate (Niranjan). Give (us) the gift of devotion: so the Sants beg (of him). He in whose house the directions all round are the tent walls, the abode of Baikunth (heaven) the hall of pictures, (and who) fills the seven worlds alike; in whose house Lakshmi is ever a maiden (ever young), the moon and the sun are little lamps, and a plaything is poor Death, the kotwal (keeper of the city), whose tax lies on every head: such a King is Sri Narhari. In whose house four-faced Brahma, who fashioned the whole universe, is the potter who casts in the mould; in whose house Shiva, the guru of the world, who has uttered knowledge true to the essence, is a madcap; at whose door sin and virtue are the mace-bearers, Chitr and Gupt the recorders, (and) Dharam Raj, who brings the dissolution (pralay), the door-keeper: such a King is Sri Gopal. In whose house the ganas, the gandharvas and the rishis, poor minstrels, are singing; all the Shastras are players of many parts, (the world) a little arena, (and) the vassal kings speak fine words (of his praise); whose waver of the chaur (fly-whisk) is the wind, whose handmaid is Shakti, she who has conquered the worlds, whose hearth is a fragment of the cosmic egg (the earth): such a King is the Lord of the three worlds. In whose house the tortoise (Kurma, the incarnation) is the bedstead, and the thousand-hooded Basak (the serpent) the cords of the bed; the eighteen loads of vegetation are (his) flower-woman, (and) the ninety-six crore banks of cloud (his) water-carriers; whose sweat from the nails is the Ganga, whose stand for water-pots is the seven seas, whose household vessels are all these beings: such a King is the Master of the three worlds. In whose house, as close attendants, Arjun, Dhru, Prahlad, Ambrik, Narad, Neja, Siddhas, Buddhas (and) the ninety-two ganas and gandharvas are (his) play; so many beings are in whose house, (that) Lord pervades all, within (all). Namdev humbly prays: (I have) the shelter of him under whose banner are all the Bhagats. ॥5॥

Narhari (nar, man; hari, lion): Narasimha, the Man-Lion in whose form, in the Puranas, God saved Prahlad; in Gurbani, a name of God. Chitr and Gupt are, by tradition, the two recorders at Dharam Raj's court who write down the deeds of every being. The eighteen loads: all plant life; an old belief holds that one leaf of every kind of tree and plant, weighed together, comes to eighteen bhaar (an old measure of weight).
1292.2: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Do not forget me, do not forget (me); do not forget (me), O dear Ram. These hold the delusion that they are of high houses; (so) all are enraged at me. Crying Shudra, Shudra, they have beaten me and made me rise (from my place); what am I to do, O Father Bithal? If you give (me) liberation once I am dead, no one will know of that liberation. These pandas (temple priests) call me a dhed (an outcaste); your (own) honour is being brought low. You, who are called kind and merciful, proved mighty of arm and boundless: (you) turned the temple round toward Nama, and (its) back toward the pandas. ॥3॥

Bithal (Vitthal): Namdev's name for God. By tradition, the priests of a temple (at Aundha) put Bhagat Namdev, a calico printer by caste, out from before it; he sat singing God's praises at the back, and the temple turned round to face him.
1293.1: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O townspeople, my caste is well known: Chamar (of the leather-working caste); (yet) in my heart I cherish the virtues of Ram, of Gobind. Wine made with the water of the Ganga, O brother, the Sants do not drink; (yet) impure wine, or any other water, O brother, once it mingles with the Ganga, does not stay apart (from the Ganga). The toddy palm is held impure, O brother, and so (people) regard the papers (made from it); (but when) devotion to the Lord (Bhagavan) is written upon them, they are bowed to and worshipped. My caste (folk) beat and cut (hides), and carry dead cattle every day around Banaras; (yet) now the foremost Brahmins lie prostrate before him: Ravidas, your servant, is in the refuge of your Name. ॥3॥
1293.2: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Those who repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the Master of Lakshmi (Padma, Kamla), are (his) servants; (to them) none other is like him, none his equal. The One alone, becoming many, has spread out; in every heart, O brother, he alone is full. He (Namdev) in whose house the Lord's praise is written, and nothing besides is to be seen: his caste is the untouchable calico printer; in Vyas it is written, in Sanak it is seen: the glory of the Name (spreads through) the seven continents. He in whose family, O brother, the cow is slaughtered at Eid and Bakrid, (and) sheikhs, martyrs and pirs are revered, whose fathers did thus: the son so succeeded that Kabir became famed, O brother, in the three worlds. He whose kin, all dheds, still go about Banaras carrying dead cattle: Brahmins strict in their rites lie prostrate before their son Ravidas, the servant of (the Lord's) servants. ॥3॥
1293.3: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. By what devotion is the Beloved, the Master of (my) life, met? In the Saadh Sangat I have found the supreme state. How long am I to go on washing soiled clothes? How long will sleep come, how long am I to sleep? Whatever I joined together, all of it has torn apart; the shop (set up) in false trade has folded altogether. Says Ravidas: when the account was taken, whatever I had done, all of it I saw. ॥3॥

1254.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
In eating, drinking, laughing and sleeping, (the mortal) has forgotten death;
forgetting the Master, (he) has brought ruin on himself; cursed is (such) living: no one is to stay (here for ever).
O mortal, meditate on the one Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered),
and go home with your honour.
(O God,) what can those who serve you give you? They ask and receive, and cannot do without (asking).
You are the Giver of all beings; you alone are the life within beings.
Those who meditate (on you) through the Guru receive Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life); they alone become pure.
Repeat the Naam night and day, O mortal: (by it) the soiled become clean.
As the season is, so is the body's comfort, and such the body becomes.
O Nanak, that season alone is lovely (in which the Naam is remembered); without the Name, what season is it? ॥4॥
1254.2: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
I make my prayer to my own beloved Guru, that he may bring the Lord, my Husband, and unite (me with him).
Hearing the thunder of the clouds, my mind is cooled; dyed in the Beloved's love, (my soul) sings his praises.
Rain down, O cloud: my mind is drenched (with love).
The drop of Amrit is sweet to (my) heart; the Guru has captivated me, and the mind is absorbed in the Lord's sweet essence.
The bride whose mind has come to trust the Guru's words is at peace in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), and dear to her Husband.
Taking the Lord as her Husband, the woman has become a happy wife; love brings joy to her mind and body.
Casting off her faults, she has become detached; the Lord is her everlasting Husband, her unfailing married joy.
Sorrow and separation never take hold of her; the Lord God has shown her his grace.
For her there is no coming and going; her mind is steady, for she has taken the shelter of the Perfect Guru.
O Nanak, repeating the Name of Ram through the Guru, the bride is a blessed, happy wife in very truth. ॥4॥
1254.3: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With no true awareness in the Naam, they were never satisfied; acting in Haumai (ego), they wasted (their lives).
Steeped in the wealth of others, the women of others and slander, they ate poison and suffered pain.
They did not recognise the Shabad (the Word) and shed their fears and deceit; in their minds and on their lips is Maya (the world's illusion and lure), only Maya.
Loaded with a burden heavy as a python, very heavy, they died and were born again, and wasted their life.
When the Shabad pleases the mind, (life) becomes beautiful.
Wandering and wandering, (beings) took the guise of many species; those whom the Guru saved found the True One.
They did not cast off their anger and bathe at the pilgrims' shrine; the Lord's Name did not please them.
They cast away the jewel, the priceless treasure, and abandoned it; they went back to where they came from.
They became worms in filth, born of it and absorbed in it again.
The more the pleasures, the more the diseases; without the Guru, (they) did not find Sahaj.
May my awareness stay in (your) service; may I sing (your) praises in joy, and through the Guru reflect on (divine) knowledge.
The seeker is born (to the life of the spirit), the wrangler perishes; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice to you, O Guru, O Creator.
We were lowly, of shallow mind and false; you are the one who sets (us) right through the Shabad.
Where the self is recognised, there you are, to carry across; the True One, the Saviour, carries (beings) across.
Seated in a blessed place, may I tell your virtues; which of them can I describe, O Infinite One?
The Unseen cannot be seen; you are inaccessible and unborn; you are the one who masters (even) the masters.
Looking to whom could I say what you are like? All are beggars; you are the Giver.
Nanak, lacking devotion, is at your door: look upon (him); may the one Name be given (to me), that I may keep it in my heart. ॥4॥
1255.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The bride who has not known the taste of (union with) her Husband weeps, her face withered;
she has lost hope, caught in the noose of her deeds; without the Guru she has strayed in doubt.
Rain down, O cloud: my Husband has come home.
I am a sacrifice to my own beloved Guru, who has brought the Lord God and united (me with him).
(My) love for the Master is ever new; devotion day and night is lovely.
Those to whom the Guru has shown (God's) sight are set free; in every age devotion is beautiful.
We are yours, (O God); the world of the three realms is yours; you are mine and I am yours.
When the True Guru is met, the Immaculate (Lord) is found; there is no more going round in the world-ocean.
When the bride blossoms at the sight of her Husband, the Lord, only then is her adornment true;
joined with the Immaculate One, who has no lineage, she is true in the True One; through the Guru's teaching the Naam is her support.
She is set free, for the Guru has untied her bonds; with her awareness in the Shabad she has gained honour.
O Nanak, the Name of Ram is within her heart; through the Guru (the Lord) has joined her in union (with him). ॥5॥
1255.2: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Another's wife, another's wealth, greed for what is another's, Haumai, vice and wrongdoing,
ill will, the slander of others, lust and vile anger: (only) by giving these up (does one find the Amrit within).
The Inaccessible, Infinite (Lord) sits within the mansion (of the body);
the Amrit within is found only by the one whose conduct is the jewel of the Guru's Shabad.
He knows pain and pleasure as one and the same, and so the bad and the good of the world.
Understanding, wisdom and awareness are gained through the Lord's Name, in the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), through love for the Guru.
Night and day the profit of the Lord's Name is gained; the Guru is the Giver who bestows it.
Through the Guru, that teaching is received only by the one on whom the Creator casts his glance of grace.
The body is the Lord's mansion, temple and home; in it he has placed his infinite light.
O Nanak, through the Guru one is called into the mansion, and the Lord, the Uniter, unites (one with him). ॥4॥
1256.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
One who knows the origin of air and water,
who stills the fire (of craving) in the body,
if he knows the place from which beings are born,
his name is a wise pandit.
The virtues of Gobind cannot be known, O mother;
he is unseen, and nothing can be said (of him).
What can one say to describe him, O mother?
(He is) above, below, in the sky and in the nether worlds;
how can (he) be described? Reflect, and give (the answer).
One who repeats (the Name) in the heart, without the tongue,
some such one knows what the Name is like.
He grows still, beyond talking and speaking;
he alone understands who has (God's) gift.
Night and day, within, he keeps his mind lovingly fixed (on God).
He alone is a true man who is merged in the True One.
If one of high caste and family becomes (God's) servant,
then let none of you (try to) speak of (his greatness);
(and if) one from among those counted of low caste becomes (God's) servant,
then, says Nanak, may he wear shoes (made of my skin). ॥4॥
1256.2: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O physician,) one pain is separation (from God), one pain is hunger;
one pain is Death's mighty messengers;
one pain is the disease that rushes upon the body.
O naive physician, do not apply your medicine.
O naive physician, do not apply your medicine.
(When) the ache goes on and the pain stays in the body,
such medicine has no effect, brother.
Forgetting the Master, (one) has indulged in pleasures;
then diseases rose up in the body.
The blind mind receives (this) punishment:
O naive physician, do not apply your medicine.
The fruit of sandalwood is the fragrance of sandal;
the fruit of a human being is the breath in the body.
When the breath has gone, the body collapses;
after that no one takes (medicine).
Golden is the body, and pure the swan (the soul within),
in which is the Naam, a ray of the Immaculate One.
(It) has cast off all pain and disease;
O Nanak, (it) will be set free through the True Name. ॥4॥
1256.3: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Sorrow is the poison, and the Lord's Name the herb that kills it;
let contentment be the grinding slab, and charity in the hand the pestle.
Take it every day, and the body does not waste away,
(nor) does Death dash (you) down at the end.
Take such medicine, O fool,
by taking which your vices depart.
Rule, riches and youth are all a shade;
as the chariot (of the sun) moves round, (only bare) places are seen.
Neither body, nor name, nor caste goes (beyond);
there it is day; here it is all night.
Make your tastes the firewood (of the sacrifice), and craving the ghee and oil;
put lust and anger into the fire.
(This is) the burnt offering, the sacrifice and the reading of the Puranas;
whatever pleases him is accepted.
(O God,) austerity is the paper, and your Name the seal (upon it);
those for whom this treasure is written
are seen to be rich when they reach (the Lord's) home.
O Nanak, blessed is the mother who gave (them) birth. ॥4॥
1257.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In white garments, (the crane) speaks her words;
(sister,) your nose is long, your eyes black:
sister, have you ever seen (your) Master?
I fly, and flying I rise into the sky
by your strength, O all-powerful Master.
On water, on land, on the mountains and the shores I look:
in every place is the Master, brother.
He who fashioned the body and gave it wings
(gave too) great craving, the longing to fly.
When he casts his glance of grace, I take heart;
as he makes me see, so I see, brother.
Neither will this body go (with me), nor will the wings;
(it is) a joining of air, water and fire.
O Nanak, when (his) grace is there, one meditates (on him), taking the Guru as one's Pir (spiritual guide);
(then) this body merges in the True One. ॥4॥
1257.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Formless One is himself the form; he himself leads (beings) astray in doubt.
Making and making, the Creator himself watches over it; to whatever pleases him he sets (each one).
This is the greatness of the servant whom he makes obey his Hukam (God's will and command).
(God) himself knows his own will; by the Guru's grace it is understood.
(Then) this Shakti comes home to Shiv, and one stays dead while yet alive.
(The pandit) reads the Vedas and, having read, expounds disputes about Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh.
This is the Maya of the three qualities, which has led the world astray; (in it is) the dread of birth and death.
One who by the Guru's grace knows the One, from his mind anxiety is gone.
(O God,) we are lowly, foolish and thoughtless; take care of us yourself.
Be merciful, make (me) the servant of your servants, that I may serve you.
Give (me) your one treasure, that night and day I may speak the Naam.
Says Nanak, understand by the Guru's grace; (only) a rare one reflects thus:
as foam and bubbles on water, so is this world.
It merges into the One from whom it came, and the whole expanse is gone. ॥4॥
1258.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have recognised the Hukam, (God) has united (with himself), burning away their Haumai through the Shabad.
They perform true devotion night and day, and keep their minds lovingly fixed on the True One.
Through the Guru's Shabad, in loving ease, they ever behold the True Lord (close at hand).
O mind, accept the Hukam: (by it) there is peace.
His own will is pleasing to God; the one he forgives meets no obstacle.
The three qualities are all a running about; (in them) there is neither devotion to the Lord nor love.
(For such) there is never a higher state, nor liberation, for they do their deeds in Haumai.
Whatever pleases the Master comes to pass; (beings) wander by the deeds already done.
When the True Guru is met, the mind stays dead (to itself), and the Lord's Name comes to dwell in the mind.
His worth cannot be reckoned; nothing at all can be said (of him).
He comes to dwell in the fourth state, and stays merged in the True One.
My Lord God is inaccessible, beyond the senses; his worth cannot be told.
By the Guru's grace one understands (him), doing one's work by the Shabad.
O Nanak, praise the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and gain glory at (his) door. ॥4॥
1258.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Rare is the one who understands through the Guru, the one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace:
there is no giver but the Guru; casting his glance of grace, he forgives.
When the Guru is met, peace wells up, and (one) takes the Naam day and night.
O my mind, meditate on the Lord's Amrit Name.
When the True Guru, the Being, is met, the Name is found, and one stays merged in the Lord's Name for ever.
The manmukhs (the self-willed) wander, ever separated (from God); no one stands by anyone.
Haumai is a great disease; Jamkaal (death) has struck them on the head.
Those who take the Guru's teaching are not parted from the Sat Sangat, and cherish the Naam day and night.
(O God,) you alone are the Creator of all; ever you make (them), and watch over and consider (them).
Some you yourself have united (with you) through the Guru, and bestowed (on them) the treasures of devotion.
You yourself know everything; before whom (else) should I cry out?
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is Amrit; it is found by (his) glance of grace.
(Such a one) utters Har Har day and night, in the Sahaj given by the Guru, with love.
O Nanak, the Naam is the treasure; fix your mind on the Naam alone. ॥4॥
1258.3: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
I praise the Guru for ever, the Giver of peace; he is God, Narayan himself.
(One who) by the Guru's grace has reached the supreme state has been given great glory;
day and night he ever sings the praises of the True One, and he merges in the True One.
O mind, reflect (on him) in the heart, through the Guru.
Give up falsehood, (attachment to) family, Haumai, and craving that is poison; keep in your heart that you must depart.
The True Guru is the Giver of the Name of Ram; there is no other giver.
(Those to whom) he gives the gift of (spiritual) life are satisfied, and merge in the True Name.
Day and night the Lord pervades their hearts, and they stay in the samadhi of Sahaj.
(When) this mind is pierced by the True Guru's Shabad, the true Bani (dwells) in the heart.
My God is unseen and cannot be seen; through the Guru the story of the Indescribable (is told).
(When) the Giver of peace himself shows mercy, (then) one meditates on Saringpani (the Lord who bears the bow).
There is no more coming and going (for one who) has meditated in Sahaj through the Guru.
From within the mind itself the mind has met the Master, and the mind is merged within the mind.
Only the True One is truth; (the mind) is won over by the True One, having lost its self-conceit from within.
The one and only Master dwells in the mind; there is no second, none other.
The one Name is sweet Amrit; in the world it alone is the pure truth.
O Nanak, the Name is received from God, by those for whom it is so written from the beginning. ॥5॥
1259.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The ganas and gandharvas were all saved through the Naam, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
Killing Haumai, they enshrined (the Name) in the mind for ever, and kept the Lord fixed in the heart.
He alone understands whom (God) makes understand, whom he himself unites (with himself).
Day and night he sings (God's praise) through the Bani and the Shabad, and keeps his mind lovingly fixed on the True One.
O my mind, cherish the Naam each moment.
The Guru's gift, the peace of the Shabad, (is) within, and stays with you for ever.
The manmukh's hypocrisy never ends; in the love of another he suffers pain.
Forgetting the Naam, his mind steeped in the poison (of Maya), he wastes his life in vain.
This chance does not come to hand again; day and night he is ever repenting.
He dies and dies and is born again, never understanding, and is absorbed in filth.
Those who through the Guru are steeped in the Naam are saved, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
Liberated while yet alive, they meditated on the Lord's Name and kept the Lord fixed in the heart.
Their mind and body are pure, their understanding pure and noble, and their speech has become noble too.
They have known the one Being, the one God; there is no second, none other.
God himself does, and himself causes to be done; he himself casts his glance of grace.
Mind and body are steeped in the Guru's Bani, and awareness is absorbed in service.
The Unseen, the Unfathomable dwells within; becoming Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru), one sees him.
O Nanak, to the one who pleases him he himself gives (this gift); as it pleases him, so he makes (beings) walk. ॥4॥
1259.2: Raag Malar, Dutuke, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
From the True Guru one finds (God's) home, his door, his mansion, that place;
through the Guru's Shabad, pride is ended.
Those on whose foreheads the Naam is written from the beginning
meditate on the Naam day and night, for ever and ever, and receive honour in the true court.
One who learns the ways of the mind from the True Guru has his attention fixed on the Lord day and night, for ever.
Steeped in the Guru's Shabad, they stay ever detached, and receive honour in the Lord's true court.
This mind plays, bound by the Hukam; in an instant it roams the ten directions and comes back.
When the true Lord God himself casts his glance of grace, then through the Guru this mind comes under control at once.
The ways of this mind one comes to know from the mind itself, understanding by reflecting on the Shabad.
O Nanak, meditate on the Naam always, by which you will cross the ocean of the world. ॥4॥
1260.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Soul, body and breath are all his; he pervades every heart.
Apart from the One I know no other; the True Guru has given (me) this understanding.
O my mind, I keep myself lovingly fixed on the Naam;
the Unseen, beyond the senses, the Infinite Creator, the Lord: through the Guru's Shabad I meditate on him.
Mind and body are drenched when love is fixed on the One, and one stays merged in Sahaj.
By the Guru's grace doubt and fear flee, when love is fixed on the one Name.
When one does the work of truth by the Guru's words, only then is the higher state, and (true) understanding, gained.
Among millions, (God) gives understanding to some rare one; that one has fixed his love on the Name of Ram.
Wherever I look, there is the One alone; this understanding I have gained through the Guru's teaching.
I place mind, body and breath before him; Nanak sheds his self. ॥4॥
1260.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My God is true, the Remover of sorrow; he is found through the Shabad.
Steeped in devotion, they stay ever detached, and have gained honour at the true door.
O mind, (so) I stay merged within the mind;
through the Guru the mind is drenched in the Name of Ram, and love stays fixed on the Lord.
My God is utterly inaccessible, beyond the senses; through the Guru's teaching he gives understanding.
(For such a one) truth is the self-discipline, the Lord's praise the way of life, and love stays fixed on the Lord.
The True One himself is the Shabad, himself the teaching, (for those) who have merged their light in the Light.
The body is frail, and the breath plays it; through the Guru, Amrit is received.
He himself fashions, and sets all to their work; that True One pervades (all).
O Nanak, without the Name no one is anything; through the Name (God) gives glory. ॥4॥
1260.3: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The poison of Haumai has bewitched the mind, which is loaded with a burden heavy as a python.
(One who) put the Shabad, the Garur (antidote), in his mouth, the Lord has killed his poison of Haumai.
O mind, Haumai and attachment are a heavy pain;
this world, this world-ocean, cannot be crossed (with them); through the Guru, cross over in the boat of (the Name of) the Lord.
The spread of attachment to Maya of the three qualities is at work in all that has form.
The quality of turiya is found in the Sat Sangat; the Gracious One carries (one) across.
(As) the scent of sandalwood is fragrant, and its rich fragrance spreads far,
(so) the way of life of the Lord's servants is noble; they spread the Lord's praise in the world.
Show grace, show grace, O my Master: set the Lord, Har Har Har, in (my) heart.
O Nanak, (one who) has found the Perfect True Guru has repeated in the mind the Name of Murari (the foe of the demon Mur, God). ॥4॥
1261.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Is this mind a householder, or is it an udasi (one who has renounced the world)?
Or is this mind beyond caste, ever imperishable?
Is this mind restless, or is this mind dispassionate?
From where has possessiveness come to cling to this mind?
O pandit, reflect on this mind;
why read so much else? (You only) carry a load.
The Creator has fastened the possessiveness of Maya (on beings);
issuing this Hukam, he brought forth the creation.
By the Guru's grace understand (this), brothers,
and stay for ever in the Lord's refuge.
He alone is a pandit who sets down the bundle of the three qualities,
and day and night speaks the one Naam.
He takes the True Guru's teaching,
(and) lays his head before the True Guru.
He stays ever apart, free of desire;
such a pandit is accepted in the (Lord's) court.
He proclaims the One, the only One, in all;
when he sees the One alone, then he knows the One alone.
The one whom he forgives, he unites (with himself);
(for him) there is peace for ever, here and hereafter.
Says Nanak, what way can anyone take, what can anyone do?
He alone is freed on whom (God's) grace falls;
he sings the Lord's praises day and night,
and then the Shastras and the Vedas no longer cry out (to him). ॥5॥
1261.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Wandering and wandering, the manmukh is made to roam through the species;
Jamkaal strikes (him) every day; (he) has lost his honour.
Serving the True Guru has ended subjection to Jam;
the Lord God is met, and (his) mansion, (his) home, is found.
O mortal, meditate on the Naam through the Guru.
The treasure of human birth, lost in double-mindedness, goes for a shell.
When (God) shows grace, love (for him) takes hold through the Guru;
(O mortal,) enshrine devotion to the Lord, Har Har, within, in your heart.
(He) is the one who carries (one) across the world-ocean through the Shabad;
(such a one) is seen to be true at the true door.
(Those who) performed many rites but did not find the True Guru
have strayed in doubt without the Guru, in much Maya;
they have swelled their Haumai, possessiveness and great attachment;
in the love of another the manmukh has suffered pain.
The Creator himself is inaccessible and unfathomable;
through the Guru's Shabad one should meditate (on him): (this is) the true profit.
The Lord, free of all need, is present, here before us.
O Nanak, through the Guru (one) merges in the Naam. ॥4॥
1262.1: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who hold to the Guru's teaching are liberated while yet alive;
in devotion to the Lord they stay awake, night and day, for ever.
Shedding their self, they serve the True Guru;
I ever fall at the feet of those servants (of God).
I live, ever singing of the Lord's virtues;
the Guru's Shabad is sweet, of supreme relish; through the Lord's Name I have gained liberation, the higher state.
Attachment to Maya is ignorance, pitch darkness;
the foolish, ignorant manmukhs are enticed (by it).
Day and night (their life) goes by as they busy themselves with worldly affairs;
they die and die and are born again, and punishment comes to them.
The Gurmukh keeps his mind lovingly fixed on the Name of Ram;
he does not cling to the greed for what is false.
Whatever comes to pass, (he accepts it) in Sahaj, with love;
he drinks the Lord's sweet essence, savouring it with his tongue.
Among millions, (God) gives understanding to some rare one;
he himself forgives, and gives glory.
One who is united (with him) from the beginning is not parted (from him);
O Nanak, (he) stays merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1262.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everyone utters the Naam with the tongue;
(but) only if one serves the True Guru does one find the Naam.
He breaks his bonds and dwells in the home of liberation;
through the Guru's Shabad he sits, steady, in his own home.
O my mind, why should one be resentful?
In Kalyug (the dark age) the Name of Ram is the profit; through the Guru's teaching one should cherish it in the heart, night and day.
The rain-bird cries out moment by moment;
without seeing the Beloved, it gets no sleep;
this separation cannot be borne.
When the True Guru is met, then (the Beloved) is met, with ease and love.
One without the Naam perishes and suffers pain;
burnt by craving, he is not rid of his hunger.
Without good fortune the Naam is not found;
(one) grows weary performing rites in many ways.
(Caught) in the three qualities, (one) reflects on the words of the Vedas;
(on him is) the filth of the poison (of Maya), and in that poison is his trade;
(such people) die and are born, and are ruined again and again.
Through the Guru, enshrine in your heart the quality of turiya.
One who honours the Guru is honoured by everyone;
through the Guru's words (his) mind grows cool.
In all four ages (he has) glory; that servant is pure.
O Nanak, rare is (such) a Gurmukh. ॥5॥
1262.3: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Night and day I have meditated on the Lord, Har Har, in my heart; with an understanding shaped by the Guru's teaching, I have put sorrow out of mind.
The bonds of all hopes and desires have broken; the Lord God, Har Har, has shown grace.
My eyes are fixed in a steady gaze on the Lord, Har Har;
seeing the True Guru my mind has blossomed: the servant has met the Lord, Banwari.
The one who has forgotten such a Name of my Lord, Har Har: a stain has fallen on his family.
O Lord, let no birth take place in his family; make his mother a widow.
O Lord, Har Har, bring and unite (me with) the holy Guru, who keeps the Lord in his heart day and night.
When the Guru is seen, the Guru's Sikh blossoms, as a child does on seeing its mother.
The bride and the Husband dwell together in one (place), but between (them) stands the hard wall of Haumai.
The Perfect Guru has broken down the wall of Haumai, and servant Nanak has met Banwari. ॥4॥
1263.1: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Ganga, the Jamuna, the Godavari and the Saraswati: these strive for the dust of (the feet of) the Saadh (the holy one).
(They say:) Filled with the filth of sins, (people) plunge into us; the dust of the Saadh's feet takes away our filth.
(It is as if) I have bathed at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage:
the dust of the Sat Sangat has flown up and fallen into (my) eyes, and has taken away all the filth of evil-mindedness.
The Jahnavi (the Ganga) was brought down by the austerity of Bhagirath; Kedar was established by Mahesh;
Kashi, and (the land where) Krishna grazed the cows: (these) gained glory by meeting the Lord's servants.
As many places of pilgrimage as the gods have established, every one of them longs for the dust of the Saadh's feet.
When the Lord's Sant, the holy Guru, meets them, they take the dust of his feet and put it on their faces.
However vast your creation, O my Master, all of it longs for the dust of the Saadh's feet.
O Nanak, the one on whose forehead it is written: to him the Lord gives the Saadh's dust, and carries him across. ॥4॥
1263.2: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
To that servant the Lord tastes sweet, on whom the Lord, Har Har, shows grace.
The one who utters the Lord's praises is rid of hunger and of every pain.
O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har Har: (by it, one) is saved.
One who hears the Guru's words with his ears and meditates crosses the world-ocean.
I am a slave bought in the market by that servant on whom the Lord, Har Har, shows grace.
Meeting the Lord's servant, one finds peace; he takes away all the filth of evil-mindedness.
The Lord's servant hungers for the Lord; the servant is satisfied when he reflects on the Lord's virtues.
The Lord's servant is a fish whose water is the Lord; forgetting the Lord, he bursts and dies.
He who has kindled this love knows it, or the one in whose mind he places it.
Servant Nanak finds peace on seeing the Lord, and all the hunger of his body departs. ॥4॥
1263.3: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
As many beings and creatures as God has made, on the head of each he writes its work.
To his servant the Lord has given glory: the Lord sets his servant to the Lord's work.
The True Guru makes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm (within).
Speak (the Name of) the Lord, Sikhs of the Guru, my brothers: the Lord carries the world across the fearsome world-ocean.
The servant who worships the Guru and serves him is dear to my Lord God.
Worship the True Guru: (this is) the Lord's service; showing grace, (God) himself carries (one) across.
Gone astray in doubt, the ignorant and blind wander and wander, and have flowers plucked (for worship);
they worship the lifeless and bow at tombs; (such a one) wastes all his labour in vain.
He who knows God should be called the True Guru; he makes (all) hear the story of the Lord, Har Har.
Before that Guru set, with faith, clothes and food, silks and fine robes of many kinds; the merit of that never runs short.
The True Guru is the Divine One, the manifest image of the Lord, who speaks words of Amrit.
O Nanak, good is the fortune of that servant who fixes his mind on the Lord's feet. ॥5॥
1264.1: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those in whose hearts my True Guru dwells are Sants, good in every way.
At the sight of them my mind blossoms; I am ever a sacrifice to them.
O wise one, speak (the Name of) the Lord day and night.
All the craving and hunger of those is gone who, through the Guru's teaching, eat the sweet essence of Ram.
The Lord's servants, the Saadhs, are (true) friends, meeting whom doubt is removed.
As the swan picks out water from milk and sets them apart, so the Saadh picks out Haumai and envy and drives them from the body.
Those who have no love for the Lord in their hearts are deceitful men; they ever practise deceit.
What can anyone give them, what can he feed them? They themselves sow, and they themselves eat.
The mark of the Lord is the very mark of the Lord's servant; the Lord himself places himself within his servant.
Blessed, blessed is Guru Nanak, who sees all alike, who has crossed beyond slander and praise, and carries (others) across. ॥4॥
1264.2: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord's Name is inaccessible, beyond the senses, and sublime; by the Lord's grace I have repeated it.
By great good fortune I have found the Sat Sangat of the Saadh; in the Saadh's company I have crossed over.
Bliss has come to my mind, night and day;
by the Guru's grace I have repeated the Lord's Name, and the doubt and fear of my mind are gone.
Those who have sung of the Lord, those who have repeated (his Name): O Lord, in your mercy, unite (me with) their company.
Beholding them, I have found peace; pain and the disease of Haumai are gone.
Those who meditate on the Naam in the heart night and day: their whole life has borne fruit.
They themselves have crossed over and carried the whole world across, and their whole family too has crossed over.
(O God,) you yourself made the whole world, and you yourself have brought it under your sway.
God has shown grace to servant Nanak, and pulled him out as he was drowning in poison. ॥4॥
1265.1: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
(One who) has not drunk the Amrit by the Guru's grace is not rid of craving and hunger.
The foolish manmukh burns in pride, and suffers pain in Haumai.
Coming and going, he has wasted his life in vain; when pain strikes, he repents.
They do not remember the One from whom they came: cursed is (such) living, cursed (such) eating.
O mortal, meditate on the Naam through the Guru.
(On whom) the Lord, Har Har, shows grace, him he unites with the Guru, and he merges in the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The manmukh's life has gone to waste; coming and going, he is put to shame.
The proud are drowned in lust and anger; (such a one) burns away in Haumai.
They gain neither spiritual attainment nor understanding; their mind is dull, and in the waves of greed they suffer pain.
Without the Guru they have suffered great pain; seized by the messengers of Jam, they wail.
(He) has found the Lord's Name, which is beyond the senses, through the Guru, in Sahaj, with love.
The treasure of the Naam has come to dwell within his heart, and his tongue sings the Lord's praises.
He stays ever in bliss, day and night, his mind lovingly fixed on the one Shabad.
In Sahaj he has found the treasure of the Naam; this is the greatness of the True Guru.
It is from the True Guru that the Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell in my mind; ever am I a sacrifice to the True Guru.
Offering mind and body, I place everything before (him), and fix my mind on the Guru's feet.
Show your grace, O Perfect Guru, and yourself take me into union.
We are iron; the Guru is the boat, the ship, that carries Nanak across. ॥4॥
1265.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 3, Partal, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Lord's servants speak the Name of Sri Ram, joining your Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), O Lord.
Trade in the Lord's wealth, gather the Lord's wealth, on which no thief can lay a hand.
The chatrik (rain-bird) and the peacock call out day and night, hearing the thunder of the clouds.
Whatever deer, fish and birds call out, they repeat no other but the Lord.
O Nanak, for the servants who have sung the Lord's praise, all the clamour of Jam is ended. ॥4॥
1265.3: Raag Malar, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Uttering Ram, Ram again and again, the fortunate search (for him).
If anyone shows (me) the Lord's path, I fall at his feet.
The Lord is my friend and helper; my love is fixed on the Lord.
I sing of the Lord, I speak of the Lord; any other love, of duality, I have given up.
My Beloved, who enchants the mind, is Ram, the Lord, supreme bliss, beyond attachment.
Nanak lives by seeing the Lord, if for a single moment, an instant, (his) face is seen. ॥2॥
1266.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
What are you worrying about, what are you thinking over, what schemes are you making?
Say, what need has he to care about anyone, whose helper is Gopal (the Lord who sustains all)?
The cloud is raining, O friend; the Guest has come to (my) home.
