O Master, treasure of grace, (keep) me, the lowly, merged in the Name, the nine treasures.
I have made many foods of many kinds, many dishes and sweets;
I have made the kitchen clean and pure; now, O Lord, my King, partake (of them).
The wicked (the five enemies) are destroyed, the friends (the virtues) rejoice; (the Lord) has made these temples, these homes (of the body), his own.
When the playful Beloved came into my home, then I found every comfort.
In the assembly of the Sants (I have) the shelter of the Perfect Guru; from the beginning this writ was written on (my) forehead.
Servant Nanak has found the playful Husband; sorrow does not come to touch (him) again. ॥4॥
1266.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When a child lives on milk, it cannot do without milk;
(when) the mother tends it with care and puts (milk) into its mouth, then it is fed and content.
We are children; God, the Giver, is (our) father.
Children go wrong many times, hundreds of thousands of times; (yet) there is no other place where they could go.
The poor child's mind is fickle; it puts its hands to snakes and fire;
the mother and father keep it held to their bosom, and then it plays in bliss and ease.
O my Master, the child whose father you are: what hunger can it know?
In your house are the nine treasures, the treasure of the Name; whatever (the child) longs for in his mind, he will receive.
The merciful Father has given this command: whatever the child asks with his mouth is to be given.
Nanak, the child, longs for the sight of God: may (your) feet ever dwell in my heart. ॥4॥
1266.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Applying myself in every way, I have made preparation, and cast off all anxiety;
I have begun all the work of the house, relying on the Master.
The dawn has come: I have seen my Beloved's face, and in my home are lovely songs of joy.
Applying my mind, I have made the places beautiful; I go and ask the Sants.
Searching and searching I have met the Guest; bowing at (his) feet, I worship him.
When the Beloved came and settled on the seat in my home, then I sang the song of joy.
My friends and companions grew happy: the Guru has united (me with) God, the Perfect One.
My friends and companions are in bliss; the Guru has brought my tasks to fulfilment.
Says Nanak, I have met the Groom, the Giver of peace, who does not leave me and go far away. ॥4॥
1267.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
From king to worm, from worm to the lord of the gods (Indra), (all) fill their bellies by doing wrong.
Forsaking the Treasure of grace, they worship others; they are slayers of their own souls, and thieves.
Forgetting the Lord, they die in pain upon pain.
Many times over they wander through many species, and can lean on no one.
Those who forsake the Master and set their thoughts on another are fools, dullards, wretches and asses.
In a paper boat, how can they cross the sea? In vain they say that they are crossing.
Shiva, Biranchi (Brahma), demons and gods, as many as there are, burn in the fire of death.
Nanak (seeks) the refuge of your lotus feet: do not cast (him) away, O God, the Creator. ॥3॥
1267.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who are my God's own are detached, and have renounced (all);
I cannot stay a moment without him; my love is fixed (on him).
In their company God comes to my mind; by the Sants' grace I have awoken.
Hearing (their) teaching, minds have become pure; dyed in (his) love, (I) have sung (his) praises.
Giving this mind, I have made the Sants my friends; by great good fortune, they have shown me mercy.
I have found a great peace that I cannot describe; Nanak has gained the dust of the feet of (God's) servants. ॥2॥
1267.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O mother, unite me with my Beloved.
All the friends in whose homes the Beloved dwells sleep, filled with peace.
In me are faults, (yet) God is ever merciful; I am without virtue: what cleverness have I?
I set myself up as the equal of those who are steeped in the Beloved's love: this is the brazenness of Haumai.
Grown humble, I have looked to the one refuge of the Guru, the True Guru, the Being, the Giver of peace.
In a single instant he has cut away all my pain; Nanak's night passes in peace. ॥2॥
1267.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rain down, O dear cloud; do not delay even a little.
Rain, O beloved, support of my mind, that there may be bliss, and joy in the mind for ever.
I lean on your support, O my Master: why do you put (me) out of your mind?
(I am) a woman, like a maidservant: without the Husband there is no glory.
When my Master heard my prayer, he came quickly, showing grace.
Says Nanak, my married bliss is made: (I have) honour, glory and good conduct. ॥2॥
1268.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meditate on the true Name of the Beloved.
The world-ocean of pain and sorrow comes to an end: enshrine the Guru's form in your heart.
Enemies are struck down and all who wish ill are afflicted, (for one who) has come to the Lord's refuge;
the Saviour has given (him) his hand and protected (him), and (he) has found the treasure of the Naam.
Showing grace, (God) has cut away all sins, and given the pure Naam in the mind.
O Nanak, the Treasure of virtues has come to dwell in the mind, and sorrow does not come again. ॥2॥
1268.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my God, my Beloved, dear as life,
O Merciful One, showing grace, give (me) loving devotion and your own Name.
I remember your feet, O Beloved; in (my) heart is hope in you.
I make my prayer to the Sants; in (my) mind is a thirst for (your) sight.
Separation is death, and meeting the Lord is life: grant your servant (your) sight.
The Name is Nanak's support, the wealth of (his) life: O my God, show grace. ॥2॥
1268.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Now I have come into accord with my own Beloved.
Remembering Ram, the King, I have found peace: rain down, O cloud, Giver of peace.
I do not forget the Ocean of peace for even a moment; I have found the Naam, the nine treasures.
My full destiny has come to light: I have met the Sant, my helper.
Peace has sprung up, all sorrows are destroyed, and my mind is lovingly fixed on the Supreme Lord.
I have crossed the world, the hard and fearful ocean: Nanak meditates on the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
1268.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The cloud has rained and spread over the whole world;
my beloved God has become merciful, and (I) have found bliss, joy and peace.
Troubles are erased and all craving quenched, (for I) have meditated on the Supreme Lord in (my) mind.
In the Saadh Sangat births and deaths are ended, and (I) have not wandered anywhere again.
Mind and body are dyed in the Name of the Immaculate One, and lovingly fixed on (his) lotus feet.
My own God has taken (me) as his own; Nanak, (his) servant, has come to (his) refuge. ॥2॥
1268.5: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
How could they live a life apart (from him),
in whose minds is the yearning and hope of meeting (him), of drinking the nectar of (his) lotus feet?
Those who thirst for you, O Beloved, have no distance (from you);
those who forget my beloved Ram are dead, and go on dying.
The Lord of the world pervades (their) minds and bodies; they see him ever present.
O Nanak, he pervades within all; he fills everything to the full. ॥2॥
1269.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through worship of the Lord, whom has (he) not carried across?
Those in the bodies of birds, of fish, of deer and of boars have been saved in the Saadh's company.
The races of gods and of demons, yakshas and kinnars (beings of the heavens) and men have crossed the ocean.
Whoever worships (the Lord) in the Saadh's company, his sorrows are destroyed.
Lust, anger and the pleasures of the great poison (of Maya): from these they have become free.
They repeat (the Name of) the Lord who is kind to the meek and full of compassion; Nanak is a sacrifice (to them) for ever. ॥2॥
1269.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Today I have sat down in the Lord's shop.
Sharing the capital of the Naam with (his) servants, I do not go to the landing of Jam.
Showing grace, the Supreme Lord has saved (me), and the doors of doubt have opened.
I have found God, the Banker beyond reckoning, and earned the profit, the treasure of (his) feet.
I have taken hold of the refuge of the Unshakeable, Imperishable One, and (my) sins have been picked out and cast away.
The strife and sorrows of servant Nanak are ended; he does not fall into the species again. ॥2॥
1269.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In many ways (beings) are robbed by attachment to Maya.
Among millions, rare is the servant who has long been a perfect devotee.
Wavering here and there, he has gained (only) toil; body and wealth become another's.
Hiding from people he practises deceit, and does not recognise the One who is with him.
Deer, bird and fish, lowly and base: into these troubles he comes again.
Says Nanak, O God, carry (us) stones across, that (we) may enjoy peace in the Saadh Sangat. ॥2॥
1269.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The wicked have died, having eaten poison, O mother;
he whose creatures they are has himself protected them; my God has been moved to grace.
The Knower of hearts is at work in all; then what fear can there be, brother?
He is with (us), our helper, and does not leave and go; God is seen in every place.
The Master of the masterless, Destroyer of the pain of the meek, has himself fastened (us) to the hem of his robe.
Your servants live by the Lord's shelter; Nanak is in God's refuge. ॥2॥
1269.5: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O my mind, one should dwell on the Lord's feet.
Thirst for (his) sight has enticed my mind: one should put on wings and meet the Lord.
Searching and searching I have found the way: one should serve the Saadh.
Show grace, O my Master, that the Naam, the great nectar, may be drunk.
Crying, Save (me), save (me), I have come to (your) refuge: show grace to (me), who am burning.
Take your servant by the hand; make Nanak your own. ॥2॥
1270.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To be the Lover of devotion is God's innate nature.
He has struck down the slanderers and put them beneath (his devotees') feet, and spread his own glory.
He has caused acclaim to ring through all the world, and put compassion into (all) beings.
Holding his servant to his bosom, he has protected him, and not let even a hot wind touch him.
My Master has taken (me) as his own; erasing doubt and fear, he has given (me) peace.
O servants of the Lord, rejoice in supreme bliss; O Nanak, faith has come into the mind. ॥2॥
1270.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Through the Guru, (the world) is seen to be God's expanse;
through the Guru, (it is seen as) the spread of the three qualities;
through the Guru is the understanding of the Naad (the yogis' sound) and the Vedas;
without the Perfect Guru there is pitch darkness.
O my mind, calling on the Guru, one finds lasting peace.
Through the Guru's teaching the Lord has come to dwell in the heart; with every breath and morsel one should meditate on one's Master.
I am a sacrifice to the Guru's feet;
I sing the Guru's praises night and day, always;
in the dust of the Guru's (feet) I bathe;
(so) honour is received in the true court.
The Guru is the ship that carries (us) across the world-ocean;
when the Guru is met, there is no more birth into the species.
That servant alone gains the Guru's service,
for whom it has come written, by (God's) grace, from the beginning.
The Guru is my life, the Guru my support;
the Guru is my daily provision, the Guru my family;
the Guru is my Master; (I am) in the True Guru's refuge.
O Nanak, the Guru is the Supreme Lord, whose worth cannot be told. ॥4॥
1270.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have enshrined the Guru's feet in my heart;
showing grace, God himself has united (me with him).
God joins his own servant (to himself);
the worth of that (servant) cannot be told.
Show grace, O Perfect One, Giver of peace.
By your grace alone you come to mind, and (your servants) stay dyed in your love at all hours.
Singing and hearing (your praise): all of it is your will;
one who understands (your) Hukam merges in the True One.
(Your servants) live by repeating your Name again and again;
without you there is no other place (for them).
Pain and pleasure are the Creator's Hukam, his will;
by his will he forgives, by his will he gives punishment.
He himself is the Maker of both ends (forgiveness and punishment);
I am a sacrifice to your glory, (O God).
Your worth you alone know;
you yourself understand, and you yourself hear and tell (of it).
They alone are devotees who are pleasing to you;
Nanak is a sacrifice to them for ever. ॥4॥
1271.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme God has become merciful;
the cloud rains down streams of Amrit.
All beings and creatures are satisfied;
(their) tasks have come out wholly right.
O mind, ever and ever cherish the Naam,
which is found by serving the Perfect Guru, and stands by (you) here and hereafter.
The Destroyer of fears has shattered sorrow;
he has taken care of his own beings.
The Saviour is ever kind;
ever and ever one should be a sacrifice (to him).
The Creator himself has done away with death;
O mind, ever and ever repeat (the Name of) him.
Casting (his) glance (of grace), he has kept all creatures safe;
sing the praises of the Lord, day after day.
The One Creator is all by himself;
the Lord's devotees know (his) glory.
He has always kept the honour of his Name;
Nanak speaks as he makes him speak. ॥4॥
1271.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the Guru's refuge are all treasures;
(there) honour is received in the true court.
Doubt, fear, pain and sorrow all depart
by ever singing the Lord's praises in the Saadh Sangat.
O my mind, praise the Perfect Guru.
Repeat the Naam, the treasure, day and night; (so one) obtains the fruits the mind longs for.
No other is as great as the True Guru;
that very Guru is the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God.
(He) saves from the pain of birth and death;
(one he saves) never tastes the poison of Maya again.
The Guru's greatness is beyond telling;
absorbed in the true Name, the Guru is (the form of) the Supreme God.
True is (his) discipline, and all (his) deeds are true;
pure is that mind which is absorbed in the Guru's company.
The Perfect Guru is found by great good fortune;
cast lust, anger and greed out of your mind.
Showing grace, (O God,) give (me) a dwelling at the Guru's feet;
Nanak's prayer (to you), O God, is for (the gift of) the Truth. ॥4॥
1271.3: Raag Malar, Ghar 3, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Winning the Guru's favour, I have made love with the merciful Beloved.
I have put on all my adornments, O friend;
I have cast off all vices, O friend;
O mind, you too, finding (him) in this way, shed self-conceit and keep company with the Saadhs.
(Then, within,) the drums and other instruments play unstruck; O friend, (the tongue,) like the koel, utters the Name of Ram in sweet words, and is most lovely.
Such is the glory of your sight, O Beloved, boundless beyond measure and never in vain; in (your) company the Sants too become like (you).
They utter the Name that carries (one) across the world;
the rosary of the Name of Ram, who pervades all,
(those who) turn in their minds become companions of the Lord.
O servant Nanak, the Beloved grows dear (to them). ॥2॥
1272.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(My) mind wanders in the dense forest;
it goes on, eager and yearning,
with the longing to meet God.
Maya of the three qualities has come to beguile me; to whom shall I tell (my) pain?
I have tried every other remedy, (but they) cannot take away the pain.
O Nanak, hasten to the refuge of the Saadh, and plunging into the virtues of Gobind, meet (him). ॥2॥
1272.2: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lovely and fine is the glory of the Beloved.
Haha, Huhu and the other gandharvas, and the apsaras, sing (of him) finely, with bliss, gladness and delight.
Masters of the art sound sweet strains in many ways, and show fine forms of many kinds.
Mountains, trees, dry land, waters and worlds (he) fills; in every heart the Beloved's dwelling is fine.
O Nanak, one in whose (heart) is fine faith has found the delight of the lovely Lord in the Saadh Sangat. ॥2॥
1272.3: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through love for the Guru, (I) have enshrined the Beloved's lotus feet in my heart.
Fruitful is (his) sight: beholding it, sins have gone, (all) gone;
minds have become pure and full of light.
(I) am astonished, amazed, lost in wonder;
by taking the Name, millions of sins are destroyed.
Laying my forehead at the Guru's feet, I have fallen (before him).
O God, you alone are, you alone.
Your devotees have your support alone;
servant Nanak is at (your) door, in (your) refuge. ॥2॥
1272.4: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rain down with joy, (O cloud,) at (God's) command,
that there be bliss, and all good fortune (awaken).
In the company of the Sants the mind blossoms, (as) the earth, meeting the cloud, is a happy bride.
The peacock loves the thunder of the clouds;
the chatrik's heart is set on the (rain)drop.
Such, O mind, (let your) love be for the Lord,
(and) cast off the deceit of Maya.
Meeting the Sants, Nanak has awoken. ॥2॥
1272.5: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sing the praises of Gopal every day;
keep the Name of Ram in your mind.
Giving up pride, casting off arrogance, joining the company of the Saadhs,
remember the Lord with single-minded love, O friend, and (your) faults are erased.
The Supreme Lord has become merciful;
the entanglements of the senses' pleasures are destroyed.
Clinging to the feet of the Saadhs,
Nanak sings (the praises of) Gobind every day. ॥2॥
1272.6: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The cloud, the form of Gobind (the Guru), thunders;
singing (his) praises brings peace and rest.
The refuge of the Lord's feet is (the boat) to cross the ocean; (there is) the unstruck melody, and words full of delight.
The thirsty traveller's mind is set on the pool, to take the water of the spirit.
Servant Nanak loves the sight of the Lord; God, showing grace, grants (it). ॥2॥
1273.1: Raag Malar, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Gobind, O Gopal, O merciful Beloved,
Master of the breath of life, Friend of the masterless, Dispeller of the pain of the meek,
O All-powerful, Unreachable, Perfect One, show me mercy.
Carry Nanak across, out of the most dreadful blind well (of the world). ॥3॥
1273.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The chakvi's eyes do not long for sleep; without her mate she gets no sleep.
When the sun comes up, her eyes behold her beloved, and she bows down again and again at his feet.
The Husband's love is pleasing (to me); (it is my) companion.
Without him I do not live in the world for a moment; such is the thirst that has seized me.
The lotus in the pool blossoms of its own nature, with ease, at the ray (of the sun) in the sky.
Such love for the Beloved has grown in (my) heart that (he) has merged (my) light in (his) light.
Without water the chatrik cries out, Beloved, Beloved, and laments and wails;
the thundering cloud rains in all ten directions, (but) without (the water it longs for, its) thirst does not go.
The fish dwells (in water) and is born of water alone; (its) joy and sorrow are by its past deeds.
It cannot live for an instant, the space of a sesame seed, a moment, without water; its death and life are with that (water).
The bride is far away from home, the Husband dwells in (his own) land; she sends (him) a message by way of the true Guru.
Gathering virtues, (she) makes God dwell in her heart; steeped in devotion, (she) rejoices.
All, as many as there are, cry, Beloved, Beloved; (but she who) is pleasing to the Guru finds the Beloved.
The Beloved is ever with (her), truly at (her) side; the Gracious One unites (her) in his union.
In all is the soul, and that soul is he himself; he pervades every heart.
By the Guru's grace (he) has shone forth in (her) very home, and (she) has merged, with ease, in Sahaj.
O Master, Giver of peace, set right your own task yourself.
By the Guru's grace (she) has found the Husband in (her) very home; then, O Nanak, (her) burning is quenched. ॥8॥
1273.3: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through the Guru's service one stays awake and aware; without the Lord, no one is mine.
For all one's efforts, none can stay (here); (bodies) melt away like glass in the heat.
Tell me, what pride can there be in this body and wealth?
They perish in no time, O madman; in this way the world wastes away in Haumai and pride.
Hail to you, God, Lord of the world, the Protector; he alone saves and assays (all beings).
All that is comes from you alone; there is none other equal to you.
Creating beings, you have kept (their) way of life in your own control; you yourself (give) the eye-salve (of wisdom) through the Guru.
My (Lord) is immortal, with no master, above the heads of all; he destroys death and birth, doubt and fear.
This poor world is a fortress of paper, (decked) with colours, marks and cleverness;
a tiny drop or a puff of wind destroys its glory; it is born and dies within an instant.
As a house or a tree on the bank of a river, (or as) a she-serpent's lair inside a house,
when the river turns, where are house and tree? The serpent strikes: (such is) duality in the mind.
The Guru's wisdom, and meditation through the Guru's words, are the Garur; through the Guru's teaching (he) has burnt away (the poison of) Maya.
(His) mind and body have grown cool as snow, (he) has found the True One; unique is devotion to the Lord.
All that is begs of you; you are merciful to all beings.
(We) have fallen at your refuge: keep (our) honour, O Gopal, that (we) may find the Truth.
Bound in worldly affairs, (the world) is blind and does not see; it does the deeds of a hunter.
If it meets the True Guru, then it sees and understands, and the wisdom of the True One settles in the mind.
Without the Truth the body is without virtue and unripe; I ask my Guru.
O Nanak, that (Guru, himself) God, shows God; without the True One the world is a dream. ॥9॥
1274.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The chatrik and the fish find peace in water alone; the deer delights in the sound (of the bell).
O my mother, the rain-bird has called out in the night.
Love for the Beloved never turns back, the love that pleases you.
Sleep has gone, Haumai in the body is spent; the wisdom of Truth has settled in the heart.
Flying from tree to tree and bush to bush, I go hungry; (now) I drink the Naam with love.
(My) eyes are fixed in a steady gaze, (my) tongue cries out; (I) thirst for the sight of the Lord of the Will.
Without the Beloved, the more I adorn myself, the more my body burns; clothes do not sit well on my limbs.
Without my own Beloved I cannot stay for an instant; without meeting (him) I get no sleep.
The Husband is near, but the poor (bride) does not understand; the True Guru has shown (him to her).
When (he) was met in Sahaj, only then did (she) find peace; through the Shabad (her) craving was quenched.
Says Nanak, through you, (O God,) (my) mind is content; (its) worth cannot be told. ॥10॥
1274.2: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The crane flies high (in the sky), (but) the water is in the sea;
the mountain is high, (but) the fort is in the depths below.
Through reflection on the Guru's Shabad the (world-) ocean grows cool;
killing Haumai, the path is opened.
For me, the blind, the Name alone is the light;
I walk by the support of the Name, in awe of the Guru, by (the Guru's) secret.
(One who,) knowing the level road through the True Guru's Shabad,
(walks) on the Guru's support, by the strength of the True One,
(and) cherishes the Naam through the beautiful Bani,
if it pleases you, (O God,) recognises (your) door and finds it.
Whether I fly or sit, (my) mind's thread is fixed on the One;
through the Guru's Shabad the Name is (my) support.
(On my way) there is no water, no mountain, no high ridge;
(I) dwell in my own home; there is no road there, and no one to walk it.
(O God,) the home in which you dwell, you alone know its state; no other mansion is seen (by it).
Without the True Guru understanding does not come; the whole world lies crushed under (Maya's) weight.
(One) pleads piteously and wails, (but) without the Guru the Name is not known.
If (one) recognises the Guru's Shabad, the Name sets (one) free in the blink of an eye.
Some are fools, blind, witless and ignorant;
some, in awe of the True Guru, lean on the Name.
The true Bani is sweet, a stream of Amrit;
whoever has drunk it (finds) the door of liberation.
(Those who) enshrine the Naam in the heart with awe and love, (whose) deeds are the Guru's and (whose) word is Truth,
(for them) Indra rains, the earth (of the heart) grows lovely, (and they see God's) light in every heart.
(One of) evil mind sows in barren, salty soil: such is the mark of one without a Guru.
Without the True Guru there is pitch darkness; (such people) have drowned and died without water.
Whatever has been done is by God's will;
what is written from the beginning cannot be erased;
bound by (God's) Hukam, (each being) does its work.
(One who) is absorbed in the Shabad of the One merges in the True One.
O God, your Hukam prevails in the four directions; in the four directions and the netherworlds (is your) Name.
In all, O God, (your) true Shabad is at work; by grace the Imperishable One is met.
Birth and death are seen standing over (every) head, and hunger, sleep and death.
O Nanak, (on whom falls) the true glance of grace of the Source of all delight, (he) receives the Naam, and it is pleasing to (his) mind. ॥8॥
1275.1: Raag Malar, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The soul-bird) does not know the worth of death, liberation and the higher state;
sitting (only) on the bank, she (tries to) recognise (it) through the Guru's Shabad.
O heron, how were you caught in the net?
(For) you do not cherish the Unseen One in your heart and beg of him.
For the sake of one life, you eat (many) lives;
swimming in the water, (you) have drowned in that very water.
You have tormented all creatures;
when (you) were caught, only then did you repent.
When a very heavy noose fell about (her) neck,
(she) cannot spread her wings and fly.
You peck (at the bait) with relish, O foolish manmukh;
caught as you are, you are set free by reflecting on (God's) virtues and wisdom.
By serving the True Guru, (the net of) Jamkaal is broken;
cherish the true Shabad in your heart.
The Guru's teaching is true; the Shabad is the essence;
(through it, one) keeps the Name of the Lord enshrined in the heart.
The pleasures and indulgences (of here) are sorrows ahead;
O Nanak, without the true Name there is no liberation. ॥8॥
1276.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
If there is (God's) grace, the True Guru is found; without grace he cannot be found.
Meeting the True Guru, one becomes gold, when it is the Lord's will.
O my mind, fix your attention on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Through the True Guru the true Lord is found, and (one) remains merged in the Lord.
From the True Guru wisdom springs up, and then this anxiety departs;
from the True Guru the Lord is understood, and (one) does not fall into the womb and the species (again).
By the Guru's grace one dies while alive, and, practising the Shabad, dies and lives (anew);
he alone finds the door of liberation who sheds self-conceit from within.
By the Guru's grace one is born in the house of Shiv, losing Shakti from within;
(he) tames the untamable (mind), gains a discerning intellect, and the person is united with the Supreme Being.
The world, a passing play, is heedless; (one) departs having lost the capital.
The profit, the Lord, is found in the Sat Sangat; by grace it comes into (one's) hands.
Without the True Guru no one has found (it): see for yourselves, reflecting in your mind and heart.
The fortunate have found the Guru, and crossed over the world-ocean.
The Lord's Name, the Lord himself, is (my) prop; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, is (my) support.
Show grace, O dear Lord, unite (me) with the Guru, that I may find the door of liberation.
What the Master has written on the brow from the beginning cannot be erased.
O Nanak, perfect have become those to whom the Lord's will is pleasing. ॥8॥
1276.2: Raag Malar, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The world goes by the word of the Vedas, and reflects on the three qualities;
without the Name it bears the rod of Jam, and dies and is born again and again.
Meeting the True Guru, one is set free, and finds the door of liberation.
O mind, serve the True Guru and merge (in the Lord).
(One who) has found the Perfect Guru by great good fortune meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
By his own will the Lord created the world; the Lord himself gives (it) support.
By his own will the Lord has made (one's) mind pure, and love for the Lord has taken hold (of it).
By the Lord's will (one) has met the True Guru, who sets right the whole of life.
Waho Waho: the Bani of praise is true; rare is one who understands (it) through the Guru.
Saying Waho Waho, one should praise God; there is none other as great as he.
He himself forgives and unites (with himself); he is attained by grace.
The true Master is supreme; the True Guru has shown (him).
Amrit rains down, the mind is content, and (one) stays lovingly fixed on the True One.
Through the Lord's Name (the soul) is ever green, and never again dries up or withers.
Without the True Guru no one has found (him); let anyone satisfy himself, and see in his mind.
Through the Lord's grace one finds the True Guru, and meets him with ease, of his own accord.
The manmukh is led astray by doubt; without good fortune he does not obtain the wealth of the Lord.
The three qualities are all Maya's wandering; (people) read and read and reflect on them.
(They) are never set free, nor do they find the door of liberation.
Without the True Guru the bonds do not break, and love for the Naam does not take hold.
Pandits and silent sages have grown weary with reading and reading, and with study of the Vedas;
the Lord's Name does not come to (their) minds, nor do (they) dwell in their own home.
Jamkaal does not leave (their) heads; through the deceit within is (their) ruin.
Everyone yearns for the Lord's Name, (but) without good fortune it cannot be found.
(When he) casts his glance of grace, the Guru is met, and the Lord's Name comes to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, honour springs from the Name alone, and I remain merged in the Lord. ॥8॥
1277.1: Raag Malar, Ghar 2, an Ashtapadi, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(On whom) the Lord, Har Har, shows grace, (him) he sets to the Guru's work;
taking away (his) pain, he makes the Lord's Name dwell (in him);
(this is) the true state: he fixes (his) mind on the True One,
(and) through the Shabad makes (him) hear the Bani of the Guru.
O my mind, serve the Lord, Har Har: he is the treasure.
By the Guru's grace the wealth of the Lord is found, and night and day the mind is fixed in Sahaj.
If a woman adorns herself without her husband,
she is called one of bad conduct, and is ever disgraced.
Such is the manmukh's conduct, in vain:
forgetting the Naam, (they) press (on others) many rites.
The adornment of the Gurmukh bride is fitting;
through the Shabad she has kept the Husband enshrined in her heart;
killing Haumai, she recognises the One;
that woman is called glorious.
Without the Guru, the Giver, no one has found (him);
the manmukh is lured by greed and duality.
O wise ones, let anyone understand this:
without meeting the Guru there is no liberation.
Everyone talks and talks (of devotion);
(but) without the mind dying, there is no devotion.
With wisdom in the intellect the lotus (of the heart) blossoms;
in that heart dwells the Naam, the Naam alone.
Everyone performs devotion in Haumai;
(so) the mind is not drenched (with love), nor is there peace.
Talking and talking, (one) makes a show of oneself;
(his) devotion is fruitless, and he wastes his whole life.
Those devotees are pleasing to the True Guru's mind
who stay lovingly fixed on the Naam night and day.
They ever see the Naam present before them;
through the Guru's Shabad, (he) is seen pervading everywhere.
He himself forgives and gives (his) love;
Haumai is a great disease in the world;
by the Guru's grace this disease departs.
O Nanak, (one) merges in the True One, in Truth itself. ॥8॥
1278.1: Raag Malar, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The Beloved is the Giver of love and devotion;
he is dyed (in love) with his own servants.
Dyed with his servants day and night, he does not slip from (their) minds for even an instant.
Gopal, the treasure of virtues, is ever with (them); all virtues are in the Lord of the world.
He has enchanted (their) minds with his feet; his servants are intoxicated with the relish of the Name.
O Nanak, the Beloved is merciful for ever; among millions, (only) some rare one has known (him).
O Beloved, your state is beyond reach and beyond limit;
you have carried across even the greatest sinners.
O Purifier of the fallen, Lover of devotion, O Master, Ocean of mercy!
In the company of the Sants, worship (him) without reserve; ever remember the Knower of hearts.
Those who wandered through the wombs for millions of births have been carried across by remembering the Name.
Nanak thirsts for the sight of (you); O dear Lord, take (him) into your own care.
(My) mind is merged in the Lord's lotus feet;
O God, (you are) the water, and your servants are the fish.
O dear God, the water and the fish are you alone; no other, apart (from you), is known.
Take (me) by the arm, give (me) the Naam; by your grace (alone) is honour received.
In the Saadh Sangat, with single-minded love, worship Gobind, merciful to the meek.
Nanak, without a master and lowly, (came to) his refuge; showing mercy, (God) has made (him) his own.
He has united his own self with himself,
the Lord King, the Destroyer of doubt.
The wondrous Master, the Knower of hearts, the treasure of virtues, has met (his) beloved ones;
great joy and peace have welled up (in them); day after day (they) have cherished the virtues of Gobind.
Meeting (him), they are made beautiful in (his) company; beholding (him), they are enraptured: they have received what was written (for them) before.
Nanak prays: (I take) the refuge of those who have meditated on the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1278.2: Malar ki Vaar: by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Rana Kailas and Malde.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When the Guru is met, the mind blossoms, as the earth is adorned when the rain has fallen;
all (the land) looks green, and the lakes and pools are filled to the brim.
The inner self is steeped in the love of the True One, like the deep red of madder;
the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, the True One (dwells) in the mind, and through the Guru's Shabad (one is) delighted.
The manmukh is on the other side: look and see with care.
(He is) like a deer caught in a snare; Jamkaal is seen over (his) head.
Hunger, craving, evil slander, lust and terrible anger (torment him);
with these eyes (this state) is not seen, as long as (he) does not reflect through the Shabad.
(O God,) when it pleases you, (these eyes) are contented, and the snare of household cares is ended.
By serving the Guru the capital is kept safe; the Guru's ladder (is) the ship.
O Nanak, she who holds fast (to it) obtains the essence; (O Lord,) you, the True One, (dwell) in (her) mind for ever. ॥1॥
1279.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is one level road, one door; by the Guru's ladder (one reaches one's) own true place.
O Nanak, the Master is beautiful; all comforts lie in the true Name. ॥2॥
1279.2: He himself fashioned himself, and recognised himself.
Parting the sky from the earth, he has stretched out (the sky as) a canopy.
Holding up the heavens without pillars, he has made (his) Word (his Hukam) the sign (of his rule).
Creating the sun and the moon, he has set (his) light in them.
He has made night and day, (his) wondrous plays.
Pilgrimages, religious duties, reflection, and bathing at the holy festivals (are of his making too).
(O God,) none other is equal to you: what can be said to describe (you)?
(Your) dwelling is on the true throne; all others come and go. ॥1॥
1279.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, if it rains in Sawan, four are filled with joy:
snakes, deer, fish, and the lovers of pleasure who have wealth at home. ॥1॥
1279.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, if it rains in Sawan, four suffer separation:
the oxen (the sons of cows), the poor, the wayfarer, and the one who is a servant. ॥2॥
1279.5: You are the True One, the Master of truth, who has made the truth prevail.
You sat in deep absorption (in yourself), the lotus (of creation) (still) kept hidden;
Brahma, calling himself great, did not find (your) end.
He has no father, no mother: who gave birth to you?
He has no form, no outline; all colours (are his).
He has no hunger, no thirst; (he is ever) filled and content.
Merging himself in the Guru, he has spread the Shabad abroad.
(One who is) content in the True One alone merges in the True One. ॥2॥
1279.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The physician was called in to give treatment; he takes the arm and feels (for the pulse).
The simple physician does not know that the ache is in the heart. ॥1॥
1279.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
O physician, you are a physician, a skilled physician: first recognise the disease;
seek out such a medicine as will rid (one) of the whole heap of diseases,
the medicine by which diseases are lifted, and peace comes to dwell in the body.
Says Nanak, if you rid yourself of your own disease, then call yourself a physician. ॥2॥
1279.8: He created the gods Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh (Shiva).
To Brahma he gave the Vedas, and set (him) to worship.
Among the ten avatars came Ram the king;
rushing (on them), he slew the demons: all of it by (God's) Hukam.
Isa and Mahesar (Shiva in his forms) served (him), (but) they did not find his end.
Setting (on it his) true worth, he has fashioned (his) throne;
setting the world to its tasks, he has hidden himself.
Dharam (righteousness) has (beings) do their deeds: so (he) has commanded from the source. ॥3॥
1280.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Sawan has come, O friend: keep the Husband in your hearts.
O Nanak, the forsaken brides, who have fallen in love with others, pine away and die. ॥1॥
1280.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Sawan has come, O friend; the cloud is about to rain.
O Nanak, let the happy wives who love their Husband sleep in peace. ॥2॥
1280.3: He himself has set the wrestling match going and made the arena.
(The wrestlers) have come down (into it) with a clamour; the Gurmukh is in full vigour.
The manmukhs, the foolish weaklings, he has thrown down and beaten.
He himself wrestles, he himself strikes down; he himself has staged the event.
The One is the Master of all; through the Guru he is known.
By his Hukam he writes the destiny on (each) head, without pen or inkpot.
Union (with him comes) in the Sat Sangat, where the Lord's praises are ever told.
O Nanak, praising the true Shabad, one recognises the True One. ॥4॥
1280.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Bending low and lower, (the cloud) has come, showing many colours.
What do I know of how (my) love for that King will last?
Love has lasted for those brides in whose minds are awe and love.
O Nanak, those without awe and love find no peace in their bodies. ॥1॥
1280.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Bending low and lower, (the cloud) has come; clear water rains down.
O Nanak, pain clings to those brides whose minds are broken off from the Husband. ॥2॥
1280.6: Creating both sides, the One pervades (them).
Spreading the word of the Vedas, he has put strife within (them).
Pravirti and nirvirti (involvement in the world and withdrawal from it) are the two sides; between them Dharam goes about as the guide.
The manmukhs are unripe and false; they have surely lost (the game) in the Lord's court.
Those who follow the Guru's teaching are heroes through the Shabad, who have killed lust and anger.
Within the mansion of the True One, they are adorned through the Shabad.
Those devotees are pleasing to you, (O God,) who are in love with the true Name.
Those who serve their own True Guru: to them I am a sacrifice. ॥5॥
1280.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Bending low and lower, (the cloud) has come; it rains in a steady downpour.
O Nanak, she who walks in her Husband's will enjoys delight for ever. ॥1॥
1280.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Why do you rise again and again to look, poor wretches? Nothing is in this cloud's hands.
Keep in your minds the One who has sent this cloud.
He alone will enshrine him in (his) mind, on whom (the Lord) casts (his) glance of grace.
O Nanak, without (his) glance of grace, all (the world) pleads and laments. ॥2॥
1280.9: One should ever serve that Lord who takes no time to create.
Having made the outspread skies, he can tear down and build up again in an instant.
Having created the world himself, he reflects on his creation.
Hereafter the manmukh is called to account, and is beaten hard.
The Gurmukh's account is settled with honour; (the Lord) bestows on (him) treasures of praise.
There no hand can reach, and no cry or wail is heard.
There the True Guru is the friend, and at the very last he pulls (one) out.
For these beings there is no other service (of worth); over (their) heads is the True Guru, the Creator. ॥6॥
1281.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O rain-bird, the One you call out for, everyone longs for.
Showing his own grace he will rain, and forest and grass turn green.
By the Guru's grace (he) is found; some rare one understands (this).
Sitting and standing, one should meditate (on him) day after day; (then) there is peace for ever and ever.
O Nanak, Amrit ever rains down; through the Guru that Lord gives (it). ॥1॥
1281.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The earth has grown distressed, and prays with (its) mind fixed (on him);
the True One listened, giving ear, and gives comfort with ease, of his own accord.
He commanded Indra, and (he) rained in torrents.
The wealth of grain springs up in great abundance; its worth cannot be told.
O Nanak, praise the Name (of the One) who gives all beings their sustenance, bringing it to them,
eating which, peace wells up, and pain does not come to touch (one) again. ॥2॥
1281.3: O dear Lord, you are true, truly true; the true you unite (with yourself).
In duality (one) is on the other side; through falsehood (he) is not met, he cannot be met.
He himself joins the one (he has) parted; he himself displays (his) creative power.
(For the false) there is attachment, sorrow and separation; (he) acts out what was written before.
I am a sacrifice to those who keep their minds fixed on the Lord's feet;
as the lotus in the water stays untouched, such is the way (the Lord) has made (for them).
They are at peace and ever beautiful, who have shed self-conceit from within.
They never know sorrow or separation, who are absorbed in the Lord's embrace. ॥7॥
1281.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, one should praise him in whose power everything lies.
Serve him alone, O mortals; without him there is no other.
(When) through the Guru the Lord God dwells in the mind, then there is peace for ever and ever.
There is no dread at all, and all anxiety goes from within.
Whatever happens, happens in Sahaj; nothing at all can be said (against it).
(When) the true Master dwells in the mind, then (one) obtains the fruit the mind longs for.
O Nanak, he himself listens to the words of those whom he has entered on his own page. ॥1॥
1281.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Amrit rains for ever; those able to understand understand (this).
Those who have understood through the Guru keep the Lord's Amrit enshrined in their hearts.
They drink the Lord's Amrit for ever, dyed in (his) love, having killed Haumai and craving.
Amrit is the Name of the Lord, which rains down by (his) grace.
O Nanak, through the Guru the Lord has come into view, the all-pervading Ram (Atam Ram), Murari. ॥2॥
1282.1: How can the Unweighable be weighed? (Yet) unless he is weighed, he cannot be found.
Through the Guru's Shabad one should reflect (on him); (so one) stays absorbed in (his) virtues.
He himself will weigh his own self; he himself brings about the union in which he is met.
His worth cannot be reckoned; nothing at all can be said (of him).
I am a sacrifice to my Guru, who has given (me) true understanding.
The world is being cheated, its Amrit plundered, (but) the manmukh does not grasp (this).
Without the Name, nothing will accompany (him); he will depart, having wasted his life.
Those who are awake through the Guru's teaching have kept their house safe; the demons (the five enemies) have no power (over them). ॥8॥
1282.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O rain-bird, do not wail, do not make this mind pine; obey the Master's Hukam.
O Nanak, by obeying the Hukam thirst is quenched, and the colour (of love) deepens fourfold. ॥1॥
1282.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O rain-bird, your dwelling is in the water; in the water itself you move about;
(yet) you do not know the worth of the water, and so you cry out.
On sea and land, in all four directions, it rains; no place is left empty.
With so much water raining down, those who die of thirst have no good fortune.
O Nanak, through the Guru understanding has come to those in whose minds (the Lord) has come to dwell. ॥2॥
1282.4: Naths, celibates, Siddhas and Pirs: none has found (your) end.
Meditating on the Naam through the Guru, (one) has merged in you.
For thirty-six ages there was pitch darkness: so it pleased him.
He it was who spread out the fearsome expanse of the waters.
Beyond all count, beyond reach, the Ever-living is (himself) all.
He created fire, strife, hunger and thirst.
Death hangs over the head of the world, (for) duality has pleased it.
The Saviour, who has given (one) understanding of the Shabad, keeps (him) safe. ॥9॥
1282.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This water rains everywhere; it rains with love, as (he) wills.
Those trees (alone) are green which, through the Guru, stay absorbed (in it).
O Nanak, by (his) glance of grace there is peace, and the pain of these beings departs. ॥1॥
1282.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In the dew-wet night (the cloud) flashed, and rained in torrents;
by its raining the wealth of grain springs up in plenty, when the Husband Lord so wills;
eating which the mind is satisfied, and the way of life comes into (all) beings.
This wealth is the Creator's play: sometimes it comes, sometimes it goes.
The wealth of those who know (God) is the Naam; it abides (in them) for ever.
O Nanak, those on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace: then he places this wealth in their laps. ॥2॥
1282.7: He himself causes and he himself does; to whom am I to complain?
He himself will call (all) to account; he himself has (them) do (their) work.
Whatever pleases him, that comes to pass; the fool (only) gives orders.
If he himself sets one free, one is freed; he himself is the Forgiver.
He himself sees, he himself hears; he gives support to all.
The One pervades all; he takes thought for each and every one.
Through the Guru one should reflect on one's own self; (then) love for the True One takes hold.
O Nanak, to whom is one to speak? (The Lord) himself is the Giver. ॥10॥
1283.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The rain-bird is this world; let no one be led astray by doubt.
This rain-bird is a beast; it has no understanding.
Amrit is the Name of the Lord, which, when drunk, takes thirst away.
O Nanak, those who have drunk it through the Guru: (thirst) has not come to cling to them again. ॥1॥
1283.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Malar is a cooling raag; by meditating on the Lord there is peace.
When the dear Lord shows his own grace, then (the rain) falls over all the world.
When it has rained, beings find the way of life, and the earth is adorned.
O Nanak, this whole world is water; from water alone is every one (born).
By the Guru's grace some rare one understands (this); that person is free for ever. ॥2॥
1283.3: You alone are the Master, true and free of all want.
You yourself are everything: whom else should I count?
Man's pride is false; your greatness is true.
Making coming and going, you created the world.
One who serves his own True Guru: his coming (into the world) I count (as fruitful).
If Haumai goes from within, then what account is (left) to be reckoned?
The manmukh (wanders) in the darkness of attachment, like one lost in the forest.
Countless sins are cut away by a single particle of the Name. ॥11॥
1283.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O rain-bird, you do not know the Master's mansion; look upon the mansion and offer (your) prayer.
You speak a great deal by your own will; (such) speech is not accepted.
The Master is a great Giver; whatever (one) wishes for, that fruit (one) obtains.
What of the poor rain-bird alone? The thirst of the (whole) world departs. ॥1॥
1283.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The rain-bird has called out in the dew-wet night, in Sahaj, (absorbed) in the True One, with love:
This water is my life; without water I cannot live.
Through the Guru's Shabad the water is found, by shedding self-conceit from within.
O Nanak, the One without whom (the soul) cannot live a moment, the True Guru has brought (her) to meet. ॥2॥
1283.6: The worlds and netherworlds are countless; I cannot count them.
You are the Creator, Govind; you created (it), and you yourself destroy (it).
The eighty-four lakh forms of life on earth have come from you alone.
Some call themselves kings, khans and lords, and have others call them so.
Some, hoarding wealth, are called bankers; in duality they have lost (their) honour.
Some are givers, some beggars; over the heads of all is he alone.
Without the Name they are (mere) showmen, and (the earth) is in dread (of them).
O Nanak, the false (wares) run out; what the True One does, that comes to be. ॥12॥
1283.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O rain-bird, the virtuous (bride) has reached the mansion; the one full of faults is far away.
Within you the Lord dwells; through the Guru (he is seen) ever present.
(Then) there is no crying out or wailing; by the glance of the Gracious One (one is) delighted.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam meet (him) in Sahaj, by toiling in the Guru's Shabad. ॥1॥
1284.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The rain-bird prays: (O God,) show grace and give (me) the gift of life.
Without water (my) thirst is not quenched; my breath is slipping away.
You are the Giver of peace, the Infinite, the Giver of virtues, the Treasure.
O Nanak, through the Guru (the Lord) forgives (one), and in the end God becomes (his) friend. ॥2॥
1284.2: Having created the world himself, he reflects on (its) virtues and faults.
The three qualities are nothing but entanglement; (caught in them, one) does not set (one's) love on the Naam.
(Those who,) leaving virtues, practise faults are disgraced in the Lord's court.
They have lost their life in a gamble: why did they come into the world?
Those who have subdued the mind by the true Shabad, (and abide) day and night in the Naam, in love,
those men who have enshrined in their hearts the True One, the Unseen, the Infinite, (pray thus):
You are the Giver of virtues, the Treasure; we are full of faults.
He whom (God) forgives will obtain (this) reflection through the Guru's Shabad. ॥13॥
1284.3: Salok, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The night does not pass for the Saakats, who forget the Name.
Nights and days pass in comfort, O Nanak, singing the praises of the Lord. ॥1॥
1284.4: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Jewels, gems and rubies, all precious stones, (shine) on the foreheads
of those, O Nanak, who are pleasing to God; they look beautiful at the true door. ॥2॥
1284.5: (Those who,) serving the True Guru, the true one, have cherished the True One:
what (they) toiled for before the True Guru has come to stand by (them) at the end.
Jamkaal cannot touch (them); the True One is (their) protector.
Kindling the light of the Guru's teaching, (they) have lit the lamp (within).
The manmukhs, without the Name, are false; they wander about out of step.
They are beasts wrapped in human skin, black within.
The True One pervades all; through the true Shabad (he) is beheld.
O Nanak, the Naam is a treasure, (which) the Perfect Guru has shown. ॥14॥
1284.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The rain-bird has recognised the Hukam, in the Sahaj given by the Guru, with love.
The cloud rains in mercy, in heavy torrents.
The rain-bird's crying out and wailing have ceased; peace has come to dwell in (its) mind.
O Nanak, one should praise him who gives all beings their sustenance, bringing it to them. ॥1॥
1284.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O chatrik, you do not know what thirst is in you, (nor) by drinking what the thirst will go.
Wandering in the love of another, (you) do not obtain the Amrit water.
If (God) casts his own glance of grace, then the True Guru is met, as a matter of course.
O Nanak, (one who) has received the Amrit water from the True Guru stays absorbed in Sahaj. ॥2॥
1284.8: Some go and sit in the forests, and do not utter a word.
Some break through frost and ice to endure icy water.
Some smear ashes on their bodies, and never wash away the grime.
Some, with matted hair, tangled and fearsome, lose their family and home.
Some go about naked day and night, and do not sleep.
Some burn their bodies in fire, and ruin themselves.
Without the Name the body (turns to) ash: what can they say as they weep?
They look beautiful at the Master's door, who serve the True Guru. ॥15॥
1285.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When the rain-bird called out in the Amrit vela (the hours before daybreak), (its) cry was heard at the (Lord's) door.
The command went to the cloud: show mercy and pour down rain.
I am a sacrifice to those who have kept the True One fixed in the heart.
O Nanak, through the Name all (the world) turns green, by reflection on the Guru's Shabad. ॥1॥
1285.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O rain-bird, your thirst is not quenched this way, even if you cry out a hundred times.
By (God's) glance of grace the True Guru is found; by (his) glance of grace love wells up.
O Nanak, (when) the Master dwells in the mind, the vices depart from within. ॥2॥
1285.3: Some, the Jains, (the Lord) has set on a wild path and led astray from the very start.
The Name is not in their mouths, nor do they bathe at a place of pilgrimage.
They have the hair of their heads plucked out by hand, and do not have their heads shaved.
They stay filthy day and night; the Shabad does not please them.
They have no caste, no honour, no (good) deeds; they have wasted their lives.
Impure in mind, these men of no caste eat (others') leavings.
Without the Shabad, no one has attained good conduct.
The Gurmukh stays merged in Oankar, the True One. ॥16॥
1285.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Sawan the bride, reflecting through the Guru's Shabad, flourishes, full of delight.
O Nanak, through boundless love for the Guru, she is ever a happy wife. ॥1॥
1285.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Sawan she burns who is without virtue, whose love is caught in the love of another.
O Nanak, she does not know the worth of her Husband; all her adornment only brings her to ruin. ॥2॥
1285.6: The True One, unseen and unfathomable, is not won over by stubborn effort (hath).
Some sing the raags and raginis, (but) he is not moved by raag.
Some dance and dance to keep the beat, (but) devotion is not done (this way).
Some fools do not eat grain: what can be done with them?
Craving has grown great, and is calmed in no way.
Rites multiply among many peoples; (in them) one wastes away and dies.
The Name is the profit in the world; one should drink the Amrit (of the Name).
The Gurmukh is drenched in devotion to the Lord and in love (for him). ॥17॥
1285.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who sing Raag Malar through the Guru: their mind and body grow cool.
Through the Guru's Shabad they have recognised the One, the one and only True One.
(Their) mind and body are true, the True One (dwells) in (their) mind; true is the renown of those true ones.
Within (them) is true devotion; in Sahaj they are honoured.
In Kalyug there is pitch darkness; the manmukhs have no way (out).
Fortunate are they, O Nanak, in whom (the Lord) is revealed through the Guru. ॥1॥
1285.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(When) Indra rains in mercy, joy wells up in people's minds.
I am ever a sacrifice to him by whose Hukam Indra rains.
Through the Guru one should cherish the Shabad; I sing the virtues of the True One.
O Nanak, the servants (of the Lord) dyed in the Name are pure; in Sahaj they are absorbed in the True One. ॥2॥
1286.1: Serving the Perfect True Guru, (he) has found the Perfect One.
By perfect grace, meditating (on God), (he) has enshrined the perfect Shabad in (his) mind.
Through perfect wisdom and meditation, (he) has washed away the filth (of the mind).
Knowing the Lord as the pool, the place of pilgrimage, (his) mind has bathed (in him).
He who dies through the Shabad, subduing the mind: blessed is the mother who bore him.
At the true door he is (held) true; true is his coming (into the world).
No one can call (him) to account, since he is pleasing to the Master.
O Nanak, praising the True One, (he) has received what was written (for him). ॥18॥
1286.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Foolish are those who give caps (kulah); those who take them are utterly shameless.
The mouse cannot fit into its hole, and yet it ties a winnowing basket to its waist.
Those who give blessings die, and those to whom they give them depart (as well).
O Nanak, (God's) Hukam is not known: where (they) go and merge.
The one Name is (my) crop of Harh, the true Name (my) crop of Sawan.
Going to the Master's door, I have had the title-deed (to it) written out.
The doors of the world are so many; so many come and go (at them).
So many beggars beg, so many go away having begged and begged. ॥1॥
1286.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The elephant eats a hundred maunds of ghee and gur, and eats five hundred (maunds) of grain;
it belches, it snorts, it scatters dust; when the breath has gone, it is sorry.
The blind and crazed (world) has died puffing itself up in pride.
Only when effaced in the Master is she then pleasing (to him).
Half a grain is the sparrow's feed; it rises into the sky and chirps.
That (sparrow) pleases the Master, she is good, who calls out, Khuda, Khuda (God, God).
The mighty lion kills hundreds of deer, and all (the other beasts) follow behind him and eat.
Grown strong, he cannot fit into his den; when the breath has gone, he is sorry.
To whom does the blind one roar out his boasts?
He is not pleasing to the Master at all.
The insect of the ak (the milkweed) loves the ak; it sits on the ak's branch and eats (it).
That (insect) pleases the Master, it is good, which calls out, Khuda, Khuda.
O Nanak, the world (lasts but) four days; pleasures enjoyed turn to pain.
There are many who talk (of it), (but) no one can let it go.
Those whom you protect, (O Lord,) it does not come near; they are to cross the ocean of fear. ॥2॥
1286.4: You are beyond reach, beyond the grasp of the senses, the Master; (you are) the True One, unseen and infinite.
You are the Giver, all are beggars; you alone are the One who gives.
Those who have served (you) have found peace, and understanding through the Guru's teaching.
For some, this is what pleases you: that (their) love is for Maya.
Through the Guru's Shabad one should praise (you), with love and affection within.
Devotion does not come about without love; without the True Guru, love is not kindled.
You are God, and all serve you; (your) minstrel makes one plea:
give (me) the gift that (I) may be content, and that the true Name may be given (me) as (my) support. ॥19॥
1287.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With the nights (life's) time wanes, with the days (life's) time (wanes);
the body wears away and becomes (like) straw.
(Worldly) dealings have spread over all as an entanglement;
gone astray, (man) has lost the measure of austerity (the way of devotion).
The blind one, flailing about again and again, has fallen into the wrangle (of the world).
Afterwards (his kin) weep, (wishing to) bring (him) back.
Without understanding, nothing is clear (to them).
They weep for the dead, and weeping, (they themselves) die.
O Nanak, so it pleases the Master.
They alone are dead, in whose minds (the Lord) does not come. ॥1॥
1287.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Love has died, affection has died, and the quarrelsome enmity has died.
The colour has gone, the beauty has perished; the poor body lies in the dust.
Where did (he) come from, where has he gone? What was he not, what was he?
(He) spoke words in (his) mind and with (his) mouth, and made merry and revelled.
O Nanak, without the True Name, (his) honour is in tatters from head to foot. ॥2॥
1287.3: The Amrit Name is ever the Giver of peace; at the end it becomes (one's) companion.
Without the Guru the world has gone mad; it has not grasped the Name's worth.
Those who serve the True Guru are accepted, who have merged (their) light in the Light.
As that Master is, so becomes the servant in whose mind (the Master) settles his will.
Say, who has found peace by his own will? The blind one does only blind deeds.
(He) is never satisfied with the poison (of Maya); the fool's hunger does not go.
Attached to another, everyone is ruined; without the True Guru, understanding is not gained.
He serves the True Guru and finds peace, on whom the Lord of the Will shows grace. ॥20॥
1287.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Honour and righteousness, both, O Nanak, (are held to come) if wealth falls into one's lap.
One should not call that wealth a friend, for whose sake (one) takes blows on the head.
Those who have wealth in their lap: their name is beggar.
(O Lord,) those in whose hearts you dwell are men deep as the ocean in virtue. ॥1॥
1287.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Worldly wealth is gathered through pains, and when it goes, pains strike.
O Nanak, no one's hunger has been removed without the True Name.
Hunger does not leave by (gazing on) beauty; whenever I look, (there is more) hunger.
However many the body's pleasures, so many are the pains that strike. ॥2॥
1287.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through blind deeds the mind is blind; with the mind blind, the body is blind.
What use is plastering with mud, when the dam of stones gives way?
The dam is broken; no boat is there, no raft, and no (finding) the depth.
O Nanak, without the True Name, how many caravans have drowned! ॥3॥
1287.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Lakhs of maunds of gold, lakhs of maunds of silver, a rich man above lakhs of rich men;
lakhs of armies, lakhs of drums and spears, kings of lakhs of horses;
(but) where the ocean is to be crossed, fire and water beyond all depth,
(where) no shore comes into sight, and an uproar of wailing rises:
there, O Nanak, it is known which are the rich and which the kings. ॥4॥
1287.8: Some have chains on their necks, (held) in God's prison.
The bound are freed through the Truth, (when) the True One is recognised.
(When) what is written comes into one's lap, (then) that True One is known.
By (God's) Hukam the judgement is made; (this) is known (when one) has gone (from here).
Through the Shabad one should recognise the One who carries (beings) across the fearsome world-ocean.
Thieves, adulterers and gamblers are crushed (like seed) in the oil press.
Slanderers and the untrustworthy (laitbar) are locked in the stocks.
The Gurmukh who merges in the True One is known in the Lord's court. ॥21॥
1288.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The beggar is named king, the fool is named pandit (scholar);
the blind man is named a judge of worth: such is the talk (of the world).
The mischief-maker is named chaudhri (headman), and the false woman takes the foremost place.
O Nanak, through the Guru it is understood: this is the justice of Kalyug. ॥1॥
1288.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Deer, hawks and officials: these are named the learned (the trained);
with the snare set, they trap their own kind; hereafter they have no place.
He is learned, he is a pandit and wise, who has practised the Name.
First the root takes hold within (the ground), (and) then there is shade above.
The kings are lions, the headmen dogs;
they go and rouse (people) sitting or asleep;
the servants (of the kings) wound (them) with their claws:
O dogs, go on, lick up (their) blood and bile.
(there) the untrustworthy will have their noses cut off. ॥2॥
1288.3: He himself creates the earth, and he himself looks after it.
Without the fear (of God) doubt is not cut away, nor does love for the Name take hold.
The fear (of God) wells up from the True Guru; (by it) the door of liberation is found.
Through the fear (of God) Sahaj is found, (one's) light merging in the infinite Light.
Through the fear (of God) one gets across the fearsome world-ocean, reflecting through the Guru's teaching.
Through the fear (of God) the Fearless One is found, who has no end, no near shore or far.
The manmukhs do not know the worth of the fear (of God); burning in craving, they cry out.
O Nanak, through the Name alone is peace found, holding (it) in the heart through the Guru's teaching. ॥22॥
1288.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Beauty and lust are friends; hunger and taste are tied together.
Greed and wealth are blended into one; to the drowsy, a cramped corner is a bed.
Anger barks; ruined, the blind (man) spouts empty abuse.
O Nanak, silence is better; without the Name the mouth holds only a stench. ॥1॥
1288.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Power, wealth, beauty, caste and youth: all five are cheats.
These cheats have cheated the world; no one has saved his honour.
These (cheats) are themselves cheated by those who throw themselves at the Guru's feet.
O Nanak, so many others, without (his) grace, are being plundered. ॥2॥
1288.6: The learned man is answerable; (his) account is called for.
Without the Name he is false, and is hard pressed and distressed.
(His) ways are hard and blocked, the lanes shut off.
The True One, free of all need, (is met) through the Shabad by the contented.
He is deep, profound and fathomless; his depth is not found.
(You) take blow upon blow on the face; without the Guru no one will be freed.
Go home with honour: one should utter the Name.
One should know (him) as the One who, by (his) Hukam, gives breath and food. ॥23॥
1289.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Living beings are (made) of air, water and fire; what joys and what pains are theirs!
(Some are) on the earth, (some) in the nether regions, (some) in the skies; some stay at court as ministers.
Some have long lives; some die and are left in distress.
Some give and eat, and (their store) does not run out; some go about as beggars all their lives.
By (his) Hukam he creates, by (his) Hukam he pulls down lakhs in a single instant.
Everyone is held by (his) nose-rope; (whom) he forgives, (his) rope he breaks.
He is beyond colours and marks, beyond (all) reckoning, unseen.
How can (he) be described, how spoken of? He is seen to be the True One, truth itself.
O Nanak, all doing and speaking is (his) appointed work; he himself is beyond telling.
(Whoever) hears the story of the Indescribable
gains riddhis (wealth), wisdom, siddhis (miraculous powers), knowledge, and peace for ever. ॥1॥
1289.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If one endures the unendurable, the nine openings (of the body) are held in check;
(if) one worships (the Lord) with each breath, the body grows steady.
(Then) where has this one come from, where is he to go?
Remaining dead while alive, he is accepted.
He understands the Hukam and recognises the essence;
this grace he knows (to come) from the Guru.
O Nanak, know: he who asserts that he is will be seized;
(where) there is no I and no me, (there is no) falling into births. ॥2॥
1289.3: One should read the Name and (the Lord's) praise; other learning is false.
Without the true trade, life is in vain.
No one has found (his) end, or his near and far shore.
The whole world is in the darkness of pride; the Truth has not pleased them.
Those who depart forgetting the Name are fried in the pan.
Double-mindedness has poured oil into the blaze.
(Such a one) comes, the play breaks up, and he wanders astray.
O Nanak, those dyed in the True One are united with the True One. ॥24॥
1289.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
First (man) was conceived in flesh, and dwelt within flesh.
When life was put in (him), flesh was given him in the mouth; bone, skin and body are flesh.
Brought out of the flesh, (he had) flesh, the breast, for (his) food.
The mouth is of flesh, the tongue of flesh; the breath is within flesh.
He grew up and was married, and brought flesh home.
From flesh alone flesh is born; all kinship comes from flesh.
When the True Guru is met, the Hukam is understood; then one comes out right.
By breaking free on one's own, one is not freed; O Nanak, in (mere) talk is ruin. ॥1॥
1289.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The fool quarrels over meat, crying meat, and knows nothing of wisdom and meditation.
What is called meat, and what greens? In which of them is sin contained?
Killing the rhinoceros, they made burnt offerings and sacrifices, as was the way of the gods.
Giving up meat, they sit holding their noses, (but) at night they devour men.
They put on a show for people to see; they have no sense of wisdom or meditation.
O Nanak, what can be said to the blind? (If one) says (it), he does not understand what is said.
He alone is blind whose deeds are blind; in his heart are no such eyes.
Formed from the blood of mother and father, (yet) they do not eat fish or meat.
When woman and man meet at night, there too it is with flesh that they consort.
Of flesh we were conceived, of flesh we were born; we are vessels of flesh.
He has no grasp at all of wisdom and meditation, (yet) the pandit calls himself clever.
Flesh from outside is bad, sir, and the flesh of the home is better?
All beings and creatures have come from flesh; the life (in them) has made its dwelling (in flesh).
What is not to be eaten they eat, and what may be eaten they forsake, those whose guru is blind.
Of flesh we were conceived, of flesh we were born; we are vessels of flesh.
He has no grasp at all of wisdom and meditation, (yet) the pandit calls himself clever.
Meat is in the Puranas, meat in the Kateb (the Semitic scriptures); through all four ages meat has been in use.
At sacrifices, festivities and weddings it is thought fitting; meat has its place there.
Women and men, kings and sultans, are born of flesh.
If they are seen to be going to hell, then their gifts should not be taken.
The giver to hell, the takers to heaven: look at this outrage!
He does not understand himself, (yet) he instructs the people: the pandit is very wise indeed!
O pandit, you do not even know where flesh has come from.
From water come grain, sugarcane and cotton; from water the three worlds are reckoned (to arise).
Water says: I do good in many ways; in water are many transformations.
Let one give up all these relishes and become a sannyasi (a renunciant): so Nanak says, having reflected. ॥2॥
1290.1: What can I say with one tongue? No one has found your end.
Those who reflect on the true Shabad merge in you alone.
Some wander in saffron robes; without the True Guru no one has found (you).
They have grown weary roaming land after land, (but) you have hidden yourself within (them).
The Guru's Shabad is a jewel; kindling the light, (you) yourself have revealed (yourself).
(He who) has recognised his own self has merged, through the Guru's teaching, in the True One.
Coming and going is (the lot) of the showmen who have set up a market (of display).
Those whose minds the True One pleases praise the One, the abiding True One. ॥25॥
1290.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the tree of Maya, (grown) from deeds, (bears) fruits of Amrit and fruits of poison.
The Creator makes all the causes; whom he feeds (a fruit), that one (eats it). ॥1॥
1290.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
O Nanak, burn the glories of the world in the fire.
These wretched things have made (man) forget the Name; not one of them has gone along (with anyone). ॥2॥
1290.4: Each one's account is settled for each; (you) have set (all) going by (your) Hukam.
The judgement is in your hands; you alone are dear to (my) mind.
Death binds (one) and drives (him) on; no one will (be able to) keep (him).
Old age, the tyrant, will dance, mounted on (one's) shoulders.
The True Guru is the ship and the boat; the True One will save (one).
The fire roars in a blaze, and will blaze night and day.
Trapped, (the bird) pecks at the feed; by (God's) Hukam alone will it be freed.
What the Creator does, that will be; falsehood will run out. ॥26॥
1291.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He who shows the home within the home (of the heart) is the True Guru, the wise Being.
There the five Shabads (sounds) ring in an unbroken strain, and the Shabad beats like a kettledrum.
There (one sees) continents, worlds, nether regions, realms and spheres, and is wonderstruck.
There instruments sound high and thunderous, (and) the King (sits) on the true throne.
Hearing the music in the home of Sukhmana, (one) fixes (one's) attention in the realm of Sunn (stillness).
(There) the story of the Indescribable is reflected on, and the mind's desire is absorbed in the mind itself.
The lotus (of the heart) has turned over and is filled with Amrit; this mind goes nowhere (else).
The ajapa jap is not forgotten; (the mind) merges in (him who is) from the beginning, from before the ages.
All the companions (the senses) and the five (virtues) have met; through the Guru (one) dwells in (one's) own true home.
One who searches out the Shabad and finds this home: Nanak is his servant. ॥1॥
1291.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The world is a great flash of lightning, passing away.
I, a mere shell of wit, did not keep the grave in mind.
I am base, the lowest of the low; O God, you are the river (of bounty).
Give me the one thing (your Name); other things are poison, they do not please (me).
(This body is) an unbaked cup filled with water, (made) by your craft, O God.
You are mighty; I have come (into the world) by your power.
Nanak, the dog of (your) court, is intoxicated; may (this intoxication) grow day by day.
The world is fire, O God; cool is (your) Name. ॥2॥
1291.3: A new pauri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All that goes on is (his) play; it is told as a play.
Paarbrahm, the Supreme God, is known through the Guru.
All vices have been cast off through the Shabad, the beating drum.
In the Saadh's company is deliverance; they have become free of want.
Remembering the Giver again and again, they have enjoyed all delights.
(The one who remembers) has become manifest in the world, with (God's) grace over (him) as a canopy.
He himself forgives and unites (with himself); (I am) ever a sacrifice (to him).
O Nanak, those who please the Master he unites (with himself). ॥27॥
1291.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Blessed is that paper, blessed the pen, blessed the inkpot and blessed the ink;
blessed, O Nanak, is the writer who has had the True Name written. ॥1॥
1291.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you yourself are the tablet, you yourself the pen, and the writing upon it too is you.
O Nanak, one should speak of the One alone; why (speak of) a second? ॥2॥
1291.6: You yourself are at work (in all), and you yourself have shaped the design (of the world).
There is no other without you; you pervade (all).
Your state and your measure you alone know; you alone have set your worth.
You are unseen, beyond the senses, beyond reach; the Guru's teaching has given the sight (of you).
Within (a being) are ignorance, pain and doubt; the Guru's wisdom has driven (them) out.
Whom you show grace, you unite (with yourself); that one meditates on the Naam.
You are the Creator, the Being beyond reach, pervading every place.
Whatever task you set (a being) to, O True One, to that he applies himself; Nanak sings (your) praises.
1292.1: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I have served Gopal, the King, who has no lineage, the Immaculate (Niranjan).
Give (us) the gift of devotion: so the Sants beg (of him).
He in whose house the directions all round are the tent walls, the abode of Baikunth (heaven) the hall of pictures, (and who) fills the seven worlds alike;
in whose house Lakshmi is ever a maiden (ever young), the moon and the sun are little lamps, and a plaything is poor Death, the kotwal (keeper of the city), whose tax lies on every head:
such a King is Sri Narhari.
In whose house four-faced Brahma, who fashioned the whole universe, is the potter who casts in the mould;
in whose house Shiva, the guru of the world, who has uttered knowledge true to the essence, is a madcap;
at whose door sin and virtue are the mace-bearers, Chitr and Gupt the recorders,
(and) Dharam Raj, who brings the dissolution (pralay), the door-keeper:
such a King is Sri Gopal.
In whose house the ganas, the gandharvas and the rishis, poor minstrels, are singing;
all the Shastras are players of many parts, (the world) a little arena, (and) the vassal kings speak fine words (of his praise);
whose waver of the chaur (fly-whisk) is the wind,
whose handmaid is Shakti, she who has conquered the worlds,
whose hearth is a fragment of the cosmic egg (the earth):
such a King is the Lord of the three worlds.
In whose house the tortoise (Kurma, the incarnation) is the bedstead, and the thousand-hooded Basak (the serpent) the cords of the bed;
the eighteen loads of vegetation are (his) flower-woman, (and) the ninety-six crore banks of cloud (his) water-carriers;
whose sweat from the nails is the Ganga,
whose stand for water-pots is the seven seas,
whose household vessels are all these beings:
such a King is the Master of the three worlds.
In whose house, as close attendants, Arjun, Dhru, Prahlad, Ambrik, Narad, Neja, Siddhas, Buddhas (and) the ninety-two ganas and gandharvas are (his) play;
so many beings are in whose house,
(that) Lord pervades all, within (all).
Namdev humbly prays: (I have) the shelter of him
under whose banner are all the Bhagats. ॥5॥
1292.2: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Do not forget me, do not forget (me);
do not forget (me), O dear Ram.
These hold the delusion that they are of high houses; (so) all are enraged at me.
Crying Shudra, Shudra, they have beaten me and made me rise (from my place); what am I to do, O Father Bithal?
If you give (me) liberation once I am dead, no one will know of that liberation.
These pandas (temple priests) call me a dhed (an outcaste); your (own) honour is being brought low.
You, who are called kind and merciful, proved mighty of arm and boundless:
(you) turned the temple round toward Nama, and (its) back toward the pandas. ॥3॥
1293.1: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O townspeople, my caste is well known: Chamar (of the leather-working caste);
(yet) in my heart I cherish the virtues of Ram, of Gobind.
Wine made with the water of the Ganga, O brother, the Sants do not drink;
(yet) impure wine, or any other water, O brother, once it mingles with the Ganga, does not stay apart (from the Ganga).
The toddy palm is held impure, O brother, and so (people) regard the papers (made from it);
(but when) devotion to the Lord (Bhagavan) is written upon them, they are bowed to and worshipped.
My caste (folk) beat and cut (hides), and carry dead cattle every day around Banaras;
(yet) now the foremost Brahmins lie prostrate before him: Ravidas, your servant, is in the refuge of your Name. ॥3॥
1293.2: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Those who repeat (the Name of) the Lord, the Master of Lakshmi (Padma, Kamla), are (his) servants; (to them) none other is like him, none his equal.
The One alone, becoming many, has spread out; in every heart, O brother, he alone is full.
He (Namdev) in whose house the Lord's praise is written, and nothing besides is to be seen: his caste is the untouchable calico printer;
in Vyas it is written, in Sanak it is seen: the glory of the Name (spreads through) the seven continents.
He in whose family, O brother, the cow is slaughtered at Eid and Bakrid, (and) sheikhs, martyrs and pirs are revered,
whose fathers did thus: the son so succeeded that Kabir became famed, O brother, in the three worlds.
He whose kin, all dheds, still go about Banaras carrying dead cattle:
Brahmins strict in their rites lie prostrate before their son Ravidas, the servant of (the Lord's) servants. ॥3॥
1293.3: Raag Malar, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
By what devotion is the Beloved, the Master of (my) life, met?
In the Saadh Sangat I have found the supreme state.
How long am I to go on washing soiled clothes?
How long will sleep come, how long am I to sleep?
Whatever I joined together, all of it has torn apart;
the shop (set up) in false trade has folded altogether.
Says Ravidas: when the account was taken,
whatever I had done, all of it I saw. ॥3॥
